title: feat: raise backup password minimum length from 12 to 15 characters
body:
## Raise backup password minimum to 15 characters

### What changed

The minimum password length enforced at **export time** is raised from 12 to 15 characters. Import/decrypt paths carry no length check — existing backups encrypted with shorter passwords remain fully decryptable (backward compatible).

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `vta-backup/src/ops/mod.rs` | `< 12` → `< 15`; new unit test |
| `vtc-service/src/backup.rs` | `MIN_PASSWORD_LEN = 12` → `= 15` |
| `vtc-service/src/routes/backup.rs` | OpenAPI doc comment updated |
| `vtc-service/tests/backup.rs` | New integration test |
| `pnm-cli/src/commands/backup.rs` | Prompt text + guard ×2 |
| `cnm-cli/src/backup.rs` | Prompt text + guard |
| `vta-sdk/src/protocols/backup_management/descriptors.rs` | Doc comment |

### Why 15

A backup envelope carries the VTA's master seed, BIP-32 key hierarchy, and ACL — the highest-value secret in a deployment. The previous 12-character minimum falls below the 15-character threshold recommended by CIS Benchmarks for privileged-account credentials and widely adopted as industry best practice for secrets protecting cryptographic key material.

### Backward compatibility

Operators who created backups with a password between 12–14 characters can still import them — the length check only fires on new exports.

### Tests

- **`vta-backup::ops::tests::export_rejects_short_password`** (new) — unit test at the op layer: 14-char password rejected with error mentioning "15 characters"; 15-char boundary accepted.
- **`vtc-service::tests::backup::export_rejects_short_password`** (new) — integration test via `TestVtc`: same boundary check.
- **`vta-service::tests::api_integration::backup_export_rejects_short_password`** (pre-existing) — HTTP-layer test using `"short"` (5 chars); still passes unmodified.

feat: raise backup password minimum length from 12 to 15 characters (#875)

* feat: raise backup password minimum length from 12 to 15 characters

Signed-off-by: Yaroslava Kurash <yaroslava.k@affinidi.com>

* refactor(backup): fold the password minimum into one shared constant

The 12 -> 15 change had to be made in five places and still left seven
docs claiming 12, which is the argument for not having the number in
five places. Add
`vta_sdk::protocols::backup_management::{MIN_BACKUP_PASSWORD_LEN,
validate_backup_password}` and point every export-side guard at it: the
VTA op layer, the VTC op layer (its crate-local `MIN_PASSWORD_LEN` is
gone), and the three CLI prompts in `pnm` / `cnm`, whose prompt text now
renders from the constant too. All five crates already depend on
`vta-sdk`, so this needs no new edges.

The shared helper counts characters (`chars().count()`) rather than
bytes. `str::len()` let a six-character non-ASCII password clear a check
whose message read "at least 15 characters", since every non-ASCII
scalar occupies 2-4 UTF-8 bytes. Covered by a unit test.

Correct the seven docs that still documented a 12-character minimum:
CLAUDE.md, pnm-cli/README.md, docs/03-vtc/backup-restore.md (x2),
docs/05-design-notes/{vtc-backup-restore,backup-descriptor-pattern}.md,
and the request example in docs/02-vta/didcomm-protocol.md.

Reconcile docs/05-design-notes/vtc-mvp.md 14.1, which specifies a zxcvbn
score-3 check on the grounds that a bare length floor admits
`Passw0rdPassw0rd`. That check never shipped; the note now records the
length minimum as what is actually enforced and 15 as an interim floor.
Consolidating behind `validate_backup_password` makes the eventual swap
to an entropy estimate a single-function change.

`vtc-service/tests/backup.rs` renames `PW` off "twelve-char-pw!!" -- it
happened to be 16 chars, but every export in that file now runs through
the real guard, so the value being long enough is load-bearing.

title: fix: cut untrusted strings on character boundaries, not byte offsets
body:
Fixes the remote-DoS panic reported as **VLM-4154 / OVTC-01**, and the wider class it belongs to.

Identified by @VikramVashisth (https://github.com/VikramVashisth) during a security fuzzing engagement against OpenVTC, with a minimal reproducer and a full source-adjudicated data-flow trace.

## The reported bug

`validate_did` built its rejection message with `&did[..did.len().min(64)]`. A byte slice panics unless the offset lands on a UTF-8 character boundary, so any invalid DID longer than 64 bytes whose 64th byte splits a multi-byte scalar panicked instead of returning `Err`.

Reproduced before the fix, with the reporter's minimal input (63 filler bytes + `U+0281`):

```
panicked at openvtc-core/src/messaging.rs:800:57:
end byte index 64 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'ʁ' (bytes 63..65 of string)
```

The reachability claim holds as written:

- `message_dispatch.rs:610` calls `validate_did(&body.did)` as the **first statement** of the `RelationshipRequest` arm — ahead of `check_task_capacity` and the `MAX_RELATIONSHIPS` gate — on a message type that needs no prior relationship or handshake.
- `process_inbound_message` is awaited inline in the state handler's `select!` loop (`state_handler/mod.rs:1639`), and `main_loop` is awaited directly in `tokio::try_join!` (`main.rs:267`). Not spawned, not wrapped in `catch_unwind`.

So the unwind takes the whole client down, not one message. The payload is small and cheap to repeat, and the `seen` dedup LRU is process-lifetime, so mediator redelivery re-crashes on launch until the ±48h freshness window closes. Availability only — safe Rust throughout, no corruption, no exposure.

## Why the fix is wider than the report

`validate_did` was not the only site. `display::truncate_did` byte-sliced as well, on the strength of a doc comment claiming DIDs are ASCII in practice. That holds for DIDs we have already validated and for nothing else it is called on — inbound `from` headers logged before validation (`didcomm.rs:687`, which falls back to the plaintext sender-controlled header when the transport authenticates no sender), agent names, friendly names.

Worth noting: `settings_panel.rs:178` carries a comment explaining that an **earlier fix for this same panic class** replaced `&value[..47]` with a call to `truncate_did`. That remediation moved the panic instead of removing it, because the helper it delegated to had the same defect. Fixing the helper retroactively makes that fix real.

## What changed

- `display::truncate_chars(&str, usize) -> &str` — the single boundary-safe primitive. Cuts via `char_indices().nth()`, so the offset is character-aligned by construction and cannot panic on any input; borrows in both arms.
- `truncate_did` now counts characters and delegates the cut. Identical output for ASCII, which is every DID that reaches it today.
- `validate_did`'s `bail` closure uses `truncate_chars(did, 64)`.
- Every remaining byte-slice on a string we did not mint routed through one of the two: capability `enabled_at` off a VTC reply, the invitation timestamp off a credential, activity summaries, mediator failure reasons (two panels), the hardware token id.

`config/did.rs:315` was checked and left alone — `find("://")` returns a character boundary.

## Verification

- `validate_did_rejects_oversized_multibyte_input_without_panicking` — 2-, 3- and 4-byte scalars straddling the 64-byte cut, plus a case that fails past the `did:` prefix so a later bail arm exercises the same truncation.
- `truncators_cut_on_char_boundaries` — sweeps every width 0..25 across all three scalar widths against both truncators.
- `truncate_chars_counts_characters_not_bytes` — character semantics, including the zero-width and no-truncation cases.
- `cargo test --workspace` green (293 core + 255 CLI + integration suites), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` clean.

Not run: the reporter's `./fuzz-asan.sh validate_did` acceptance criterion. That harness lives out-of-tree in `openvtc-fuzzer`, which is not part of this repository — @VikramVashisth, happy to have it re-run against this branch to close that box.

## Credit

Reported and reproduced by @VikramVashisth (https://github.com/VikramVashisth). The report pinned the sink to a commit, traced the taint from the remote peer through both dispatch call sites, and correctly called out that a panic in a validator suggested the input-hardening boundary needed a systematic audit — which is exactly what turned up the six further sites fixed here.

title: feat(vta-service): mint the step-up approve-request as 0.2; inbound stays bilingual
body:
## Summary

The deferred follow-up to #870: the minted step-up approve-request moves from `auth/step-up/approve-request/0.1` to `/0.2`. Receivers migrated first — vta-mobile-core (#871) and the browser plugin (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#103) accept both request minors, and the webvh control plane accepts both approve-response minors (part of the signed-request-legs push, affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#147) — so this is the producer-side cutover.

### 0.1 → 0.2 shape delta (from the dtgwg specs)

The approve-request payload is otherwise identical between minors — same required members (`subject`, `sessionId`, `challenge`, `reason`), same optional hints (`targetAcr`, `ttl`, `webauthn`, `ext`), same ttl semantics. What changes:

- type URI minor bump `/0.1` → `/0.2`
- `payload.acceptableEvidence` enum spelling: `did-signed` → `didSigned` (`webauthn` unchanged) — the **only** payload-value difference
- spec error codes go camelCase (`subject_unknown` → `subjectUnknown`, …) — informational; the request leg emits none
- `ext` $ref moves to the 0.2 framework schema (no wire effect)

(The approve-response side's 0.2 additionally renames `evidence.kind` `did-signed` → `didSigned` and adds the delegated-approver `approverUnauthorized` semantics — both already handled by #870's dual-accept handler.)

### What this PR does

- `mint_pending_step_up` emits the `/0.2` type URI + `didSigned` wire spelling. **Signing is exactly as #870 built it**: `eddsa-jcs-2022`, `assertionMethod`, `{vta_did}#key-0`, proof last over the complete document including `payload.ext` — the Cierge `authorizationContext` carriage is unchanged and stays inside the signed surface (existing test kept and passing).
- The DIDComm push type for the delegated approve-request follows the document to `/0.2`.
- **Inbound stays bilingual** (approvers in the field answer with either minor during the transition):
  - the trust-task dispatcher keeps accepting approve-response 0.1 **and** 0.2 (typed dual-accept over the signed bytes — unchanged);
  - the DIDComm router's canonical step-up-approve registration now accepts the `/0.2` request URI beside `/0.1` and the legacy `vta/step-up/*/1.0`, echoing the caller's own minor in the response type (the control plane accepts both response minors).
- The stored `PendingStepUp.acceptable_evidence` keeps the internal kebab canonical form — it is state, not wire — so in-flight 0.13.17 pending step-ups stay consumable across the deploy.

### Tests

- New integration round-trip (`v0_2_minted_request_completes_with_a_0_1_flavored_response`): the real gate mints the 0.2 request, its VTA proof verifies end-to-end via `di_proof` (issuer == proof VM DID), and a 0.1-flavored signed approve-response (kebab `did-signed` evidence) completes the 0.2-minted step-up, acking in the approver's 0.1 family.
- Existing 0.1/0.2 approve-response, delegated, unauthorized-approver, and ext-carriage tests all updated/passing.
- `cargo test -p vta-service --no-fail-fast`: all green. `tests/e2e` (embedded mediator): 162 passed, 11 ignored (need the webvh-host fixture). fmt + clippy clean.
- A genuinely cross-repo webvh↔plugin e2e is not feasible from this repo; the cross-version guarantees are covered by the integration round-trip here plus the receiver-side tests landed in #871 and OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#103.

### Release

vta-service 0.13.17 → 0.13.18, root CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.

Refs #870, #871, affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#147, OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#103.

title: fix(vta-sdk): select_initial_transport consults tsp_mediator_did, and TSP provisions
body:
Closes https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/issues/869

## The bug, re-verified against current `origin/main` (433f9131)

`vta-sdk/src/provision_client/runner.rs::select_initial_transport` decided the
provisioning wire from **two of the three** endpoints its own resolver produces:

```rust
match (resolved.mediator_did.is_some(), resolved.rest_url.is_some()) { … }
```

`ResolvedVta` (`provision_client/resolve.rs`) carries `tsp_mediator_did`,
`mediator_did` and `rest_url`, and even exposes `advertised()` — which *does*
report `Protocol::Tsp` and has four tests pinning it. The selector never
consulted it. A VTA advertising only `#tsp` therefore fell through to
`InitialChoice::Neither` and failed with `"resolved (no endpoints)"` about a
document the resolver had just parsed a real endpoint out of. Everything the
issue describes is still true at 433f9131; nothing had moved.

## Decision: option (A) — TSP is a provisioning transport

Per the directive. The investigation says this is **wiring, not new protocol
surface**, and here is the evidence that decided it:

1. **`vta-service/src/messaging/tsp_inbound.rs::dispatch_one`** hands every
   unpacked TSP frame straight to `crate::trust_tasks::dispatch_trust_task_core`
   — *the same spine* REST (`POST /api/trust-tasks`) and the DIDComm trust-task
   envelope feed. Its own module doc says so, and states the ranking this PR
   adopts: "TSP is the highest-preference transport (TSP > DIDComm > REST)".
2. **Both operations the provisioning flow needs are already on that spine**
   (`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs`): `TASK_PROVISION_INTEGRATION_0_2` →
   `provision_integration::handle_request`, and `TASK_WEBVH_SERVERS_LIST_1_0` →
   `webvh::handle_servers_list`. The handler takes a `ProvisionIntegrationRequest`
   payload and returns a `ProvisionIntegrationResponse` — the exact types the
   DIDComm and REST legs already exchange. There is **no transport gating**
   anywhere in the spine.
3. **The SDK already has the client half.** `VtaClient::connect_tsp` +
   `dispatch_trust_task` route a trust task over `TspSession::request`, which
   correlates replies by `threadId` (`tsp_demux::correlates`) against the
   `respond_with(...)` documents `trust_tasks/helpers.rs::success_response`
   emits. Auth is intrinsic-sender: TSP `unpack` yields a **proven** sender VID
   that `auth_from_did` resolves straight to the ACL grant `pnm acl create`
   wrote — the same model as DIDComm authcrypt, no challenge and no token.

So this PR drives the existing surface rather than inventing a parallel one.

### Where TSP genuinely is *not* symmetric with DIDComm — modelled, not assumed

- **No handshake.** `DIDCommSession::connect` flushes the mediator inbox, enables
  the websocket and sets the client's mediator ACL. The TSP socket does none of
  that. Neither transport performs a VTA round-trip at connect time, so the
  socket open is the `AuthenticateTSP` proxy exactly as the mediator connect is
  the `AuthenticateDIDComm` proxy today. Documented as such in `runner_tsp`.
- **No envelope.** TSP carries the Trust-Task bytes directly; the DIDComm leg
  wraps them (or, for provisioning, uses a DIDComm *protocol message*).
- **Version.** The DIDComm leg addresses `provision/integration/0.1` as a
  DIDComm protocol message routed by `messaging::handlers_protocol`. Only **0.2**
  is registered on the trust-task spine, so the TSP leg uses `0.2`. The signed VP
  inside is byte-identical either way — `spec_version` only selects the casing of
  the options *around* it (`request_body_for_version`, identity for 0.2).
- **Correlation is the application's job** — already solved by `tsp_demux`.

## What changed

- **`InitialChoice` now has one variant per cell of the 2×2×2 advertise matrix**
  — `TspOnly`, `TspAndDIDComm`, `TspAndRest`, `TspDIDCommAndRest` beside the
  existing four — so the choice never discards the endpoint the runner needs for
  fallback. `starts_with_tsp()` / `has_didcomm()` / `has_rest()` keep match sites
  small, and a test asserts they agree with the resolved document (the degrade
  path `expect`s on them).
- **`select_initial_transport` consults `tsp_mediator_did`**, and is
  **feature-independent by construction**: a `tsp`-less build still selects
  `TspOnly` for a TSP-only VTA and then fails naming the cargo feature. The
  selection matrix does not change shape with the feature flags.
- **`force_transport` honours `Some(Protocol::Tsp)`**, collapsing to `TspOnly`
  — the same "forced means no fallback" precedent the REST/DIDComm arms already
  set.
- **New `vta-sdk/src/provision_client/runner_tsp.rs`** (gated on `tsp`):
  `run_tsp_attempt` mirroring `run_didcomm_attempt` for all three
  `VtaIntent`s, plus one-shot `provision_via_tsp` /
  `provision_admin_rotation_via_tsp` siblings of the DIDComm/REST entry points.
  The `#[cfg(not(feature = "tsp"))]` twin compiles and reports a **pre-auth**
  failure naming the missing feature, in the shape
  `session::connect_tsp_bounded` already uses.
- **Dispatch restructured, not duplicated.** The DIDComm and REST arms of
  `run_connection_test` were extracted into `dispatch_didcomm_leg` /
  `dispatch_rest_leg` so the TSP leg reuses them verbatim as its fallback, and
  `emit_mediator_outcome` is shared by the TSP and DIDComm legs so their event
  translation cannot drift.
- **`Protocol` gains `Tsp`**, **`DiagCheck` gains `AuthenticateTSP`** (listed
  first, so `DiagCheck::all()` renders in the order the runner tries them),
  `AttemptLog` and `HeadlessVtaError` gain a `tsp` slot, and the "advertises
  neither" terminal message became "advertises no usable transport" naming all
  three.

### Ranking — stated explicitly, because it changes a default

**TSP > DIDComm > REST.** Precedent: `ResolvedVta::advertised()` documents that
order ("in preference order", with a test named
`advertised_is_in_preference_order`), `tsp_inbound.rs` states it, and
`session.rs`'s `TransportChoice::Auto` prefers TSP for the runtime client.

**This changes the default wire for a VTA advertising both `#tsp` and
`#vta-didcomm`** — the reference topology, and `vtc-service`'s setup wizard
drives `run_connection_test` with `force_transport: None`. Two things bound the
blast radius:

- Degradation is **pre-auth only**. A TSP leg that fails before the VTA accepts
  anything — including "this build has no `tsp` feature" — is reported as an
  `AttemptCompleted` and the run continues on DIDComm/REST. A post-auth failure
  stays terminal, exactly as the existing `AttemptOutcome` split already
  dictated for DIDComm ("a different transport may succeed" / "a different wire
  will reproduce the rejection").
- `force_transport: Some(Protocol::DidComm)` pins the old behaviour.

### Selection matrix (now pinned, one test per cell)

| `#tsp` | `#DIDCommMessaging` | `#vta-rest` | `InitialChoice` | leg | fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | `TspDIDCommAndRest` | TSP | DIDComm |
| ✓ | ✓ | – | `TspAndDIDComm` | TSP | DIDComm |
| ✓ | – | ✓ | `TspAndRest` | TSP | REST |
| ✓ | – | – | `TspOnly` | TSP | none |
| – | ✓ | ✓ | `BothAvailable` | DIDComm | (consumer) |
| – | ✓ | – | `DIDCommOnly` | DIDComm | none |
| – | – | ✓ | `RestOnly` | REST | none |
| – | – | – | `Neither` | — | — |

Plus: `neither_is_reserved_for_a_document_that_advertises_nothing`,
`tsp_selection_does_not_depend_on_the_tsp_feature`,
`starts_with_tsp_covers_exactly_the_tsp_variants`,
`fallback_predicates_match_the_resolved_endpoints` (all eight rows),
`tsp_only_has_no_fallback`.

## `InitialChoice` / `Protocol` match-site sweep

Swept the whole workspace for `InitialChoice`, `provision_client`'s `Protocol`,
`ResolvedVta::advertised()`, `AttemptLog`, `HeadlessVtaError` and every
`run_provision` / `run_connection_test` consumer:

- `InitialChoice` is matched **only inside `vta-sdk`** (`runner.rs`, re-exported
  via `provision_client::mod` and `prelude`). No daemon or CLI matches it.
- `provision_client::Protocol` is matched in `driver.rs:238` — updated with a
  `Protocol::Tsp` arm.
- `pnm-cli/src/commands/health.rs` matches `Protocol::{Tsp,Didcomm,Rest}` — that
  is `protocol::matching::Protocol`, a **different** enum that already had `Tsp`.
  Untouched.
- `vtc-service` (`setup/wizard.rs`, `emergency.rs`) consumes `VtaEvent` and
  destructures `PreflightDone { .. }` with a rest pattern; it compiles unchanged
  and handles the TSP leg's terminal `Connected` on its existing arm.
- Out-of-workspace: adding enum variants is a breaking match for an external
  consumer that matches exhaustively (`affinidi-webvh-service` is the known one).
  Unavoidable — the issue asks for a new variant, and the alternative is a
  transport choice that keeps discarding the endpoint it was asked about.

## Deliberate gap, scoped

The TSP `FullSetup` leg runs the webvh catalogue lookup and the provision
round-trip back-to-back on one socket rather than splitting into `PreflightOk` →
`run_provision_flight`. That split exists so an interactive consumer can close
its session while a picker dialog is on screen, and the picker is driven off
`VtaEvent::PreflightDone`, whose `mediator_did: String` is a DIDComm mediator by
construction. Carrying a TSP mediator there means either overloading that field
(the resolver deliberately keeps the two apart) or a public event-shape change
— out of scope here. Meanwhile the TSP leg resolves the server choice the way
`run_provision` does: explicit `WEBVH_SERVER` in the ask wins (what
`vtc-service`'s wizard does), 0/1 catalogue entries auto-pick, and 2+ with no
explicit choice is refused **by name** rather than guessed.

## Needs a live TSP-only VTA to confirm

Everything below is reasoned from the sources and compiles + unit-tests, but no
TSP-only VTA was available to exercise the wire:

1. **The full round-trip**: `provision/integration/0.2` over TSP against a VTA
   advertising only `#tsp`, end to end into an opened sealed bundle.
2. **Sealed-bundle size over a TSP frame.** The provisioning reply carries an
   armored bundle (keys + `did.jsonl` + VC + trust bundle) — far larger than the
   `task-consent/request` pushes TSP carries today. If the mediator or the TSP
   stack has a frame ceiling, this is where it shows up first.
3. **`PROVISION_TIMEOUT_SECS = 60`** is copied from the DIDComm leg; TSP's
   `request` correlation loop pumps in 250 ms slices, so a slow VTA mint should
   behave the same, but that is untested under load.
4. **Whether the mediator's one-socket-per-DID ceiling** interacts badly if a
   setup DID somehow already holds a session (it should not — the setup key is
   freshly minted per run).

## Verification

```
cargo test -p vta-sdk --lib                                   224 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p vta-sdk --lib --features provision-client,tsp   512 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p vta-sdk --lib --features provision-client       499 passed; 0 failed   (non-tsp build)
cargo check  --workspace --all-targets                        Finished
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings         Finished
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                    clean
cargo check -p vta-sdk --no-default-features --features provision-client   Finished
cargo check -p vta-sdk --all-features                                      Finished
```

Both feature configurations are exercised: the `tsp` build compiles and tests the
real leg, the non-`tsp` build compiles and tests the honest-diagnostic twin.
`tests/e2e` already enables `vta-sdk` with both `tsp` and `provision-client`, so
the workspace clippy run covers the TSP leg.

**Pre-existing, not introduced here:** `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk --all-features
--all-targets` fails in `vta-sdk/tests/session_store.rs:622` (`E0004`, missing
`_` arm on the `#[non_exhaustive]` `VtaEndpoint` once `tsp` adds a variant).
Reproduced on a clean `origin/main` checkout with my changes stashed. CI runs
`cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, which is green. Left alone — no
drive-by fixes.

## Release guards

- `vta-sdk` 0.20.25 → **0.20.26** (next free patch; checked `main`, not assumed).
- Root `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## Unreleased`.
- `Cargo.lock` refreshed.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Ranking: TSP-first for a `#tsp` + `#vta-didcomm` VTA is the intended
      default change, and pre-auth-only degradation is the right guard rail.
- [ ] `InitialChoice`'s 8 variants vs. a `Tsp { didcomm_fallback, rest_fallback }`
      struct variant — flat was chosen to match the existing style and to make
      the test matrix one assertion per cell.
- [ ] `provision/integration/**0.2**` on the TSP leg (the spine registers only
      0.2) while the DIDComm leg still sends 0.1 as a protocol message.
- [ ] The socket-open-as-`AuthenticateTSP` proxy — same proxy the DIDComm leg
      uses, but worth an explicit nod.
- [ ] The deferred TSP `PreflightDone`/picker path and its `WEBVH_SERVER`
      workaround.
- [ ] Breaking-for-external-consumers enum additions (`InitialChoice`,
      `Protocol`, `DiagCheck`) on a patch bump.

Version bumps may be rebased by the orchestrator as sibling consolidation PRs
merge.

title: provision_client: select_initial_transport ignores tsp_mediator_did, so a TSP-only VTA cannot be provisioned
body:
## The bug

`provision_client::select_initial_transport` decides the provisioning transport from only two of the three endpoints its own resolver produces:

```rust
// vta-sdk/src/provision_client/runner.rs:54
pub fn select_initial_transport(resolved: &ResolvedVta) -> InitialChoice {
    match (resolved.mediator_did.is_some(), resolved.rest_url.is_some()) {
        …
        (false, false) => InitialChoice::Neither,
    }
}
```

`ResolvedVta` carries three (`resolve.rs:21-25`): `tsp_mediator_did`, `mediator_did`, `rest_url`. The resolver populates `tsp_mediator_did` from a `#tsp` service and even exposes a helper that tests it (`resolve.rs:35`), but the transport selector never consults it.

**Consequence:** provisioning against a **TSP-only** VTA — one advertising `#tsp` but neither a DIDComm mediator nor `VTARest` — returns `InitialChoice::Neither` and fails with the diagnostic `"resolved (no endpoints)"`, despite the DID document plainly advertising an endpoint the SDK just parsed.

This became reachable in the 0.20 line: 0.19 synthesised a REST URL from the VTA DID's domain, so a TSP-only document still resolved something and provisioning proceeded over REST. 0.20 correctly stopped synthesising, which removed the accidental fallback and exposed the gap.

No impact on any VTA advertising DIDComm or REST — which is why it has not been noticed.

## Why it needs fixing here rather than in the consumer

A consumer cannot route around it. `select_initial_transport` is invoked inside `run_provision`'s driver loop; short of reimplementing the runner, there is no seam to inject a TSP leg. `affinidi-webvh-service` hit this while upgrading to 0.20 (see affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#148) and deliberately left it unpatched rather than fork the flow.

## Suggested shape

Extend `InitialChoice` with a TSP arm and consult `tsp_mediator_did` in the match, preferring it consistently with however the runner already ranks DIDComm against REST. If TSP genuinely is not supported as a *provisioning* transport — as opposed to a post-provisioning one — then the honest fix is the diagnostic: `Neither` should say the document advertises only `#tsp` and that provisioning cannot use it, rather than "no endpoints", which sends whoever hits it looking for a DID-document error that is not there.

## Found by

The `vta-sdk` 0.19 → 0.20 upgrade of `affinidi-webvh-service` (affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#148), part of the Trust Tasks consolidation programme. Verified directly against the vendored 0.20.24 sources, not inferred from behaviour.

fix(vta-sdk): select_initial_transport consults tsp_mediator_did, and TSP provisions (#872)

`provision_client::select_initial_transport` decided the provisioning wire
from two of the three endpoints its own resolver produces. `ResolvedVta`
carries `tsp_mediator_did`, `mediator_did` and `rest_url` — and exposes an
`advertised()` helper that reports all three — but the selector matched only
on `(mediator_did, rest_url)`. A VTA advertising only `#tsp` therefore fell
through to `InitialChoice::Neither` and failed with "resolved (no endpoints)",
about a document the resolver had just parsed an endpoint out of.

TSP now carries provisioning rather than merely being named in the error.
The VTA's TSP inbound dispatcher already feeds `dispatch_trust_task_core` —
the same spine REST and DIDComm use — and both operations this flow needs
(`spec/vta/webvh/servers/list/1.0`, `spec/provision/integration/0.2`) are
registered on it, so the documents are byte-identical across transports.

- `InitialChoice` gains one variant per cell of the 2x2x2 advertise matrix,
  with `starts_with_tsp`/`has_didcomm`/`has_rest` predicates.
- Ranking is TSP > DIDComm > REST, matching `ResolvedVta::advertised()` and
  vta-service's inbound ranking. Degradation is pre-auth only; a forced
  transport never degrades.
- `Protocol` gains `Tsp`; `DiagCheck` gains `AuthenticateTSP`; `AttemptLog`
  and `HeadlessVtaError` gain a `tsp` slot.
- New `provision_client::runner_tsp`, gated on `tsp`. A build without the
  feature compiles and fails naming the cargo feature, not the DID document.
- Selection stays feature-independent, so the matrix does not change shape

Closes #869

title: feat(mobile): verify request proofs on-device before prompting
body:
## What

The approver-side half of the "signed request legs" programme (affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#147; senders: #870 and affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#149): vta-mobile-core's documented "hardening follow-up" is implemented. Both inbound request families are verified on-device **before** any prompt; unverifiable → typed refusal, never a prompt (the spec's `untrusted_issuer` rule).

- New shared gate `verify_signed_request` (`vta-mobile-core/src/proof.rs`). Check order: issuer present → proof present/well-formed → `proofPurpose == assertionMethod` → verificationMethod DID == issuer → **enrolled-allowlist before any resolution** (no network I/O on behalf of non-enrolled DIDs) → eddsa-jcs-2022 signature verify.
- Verification is **resolver-backed and async** (the crate's existing tokio/uniffi posture; `trust-tasks-proof`'s `CachedDidResolver` over the process-wide `DIDCacheClient` → `affinidi-data-integrity` verify). Survives VTA key rotation, unlike enrollment-time-pinned key material. Runs over the **raw JSON minus `proof`** — byte-faithful to what the executor signed, including wire fields the lenient display parse tolerates.
- `parse_task_consent_request` and `parse_step_up_request` gate on it; step-up accepts both `approve-request/0.1` (VTA) and `/0.2` (webvh control plane) type URIs, normalising 0.2's `didSigned` evidence spelling so Swift switches stay version-independent.

## FFI changes (iOS follow-up required)

- Both parse functions are now **async** and take `trustedIssuers: [String]` (the enrolled VTA DID + granted executor DIDs, held by the native layer).
- `TaskConsentRequest.issuer` / `StepUpRequest.relying_party`: `Option<String>` → `String` (the proven signer, guaranteed enrolled).
- New `FfiError::UntrustedIssuer { reason }` — the typed "drop, never prompt" signal. Other variants unchanged.

## Tests

`cargo test -p vta-mobile-core`: 56 passed, 0 failed (4 pre-existing network-gated ignored). New vectors signed in-test with `affinidi-data-integrity`: enrolled signer accepted (full resolve-and-verify, offline via did:key); missing proof, non-enrolled signer, issuer/VM mismatch, post-sign tampering → all refused; 0.2 step-up parse + evidence normalisation. fmt + clippy clean.

## Merge notes

- **Merge/ship only after the senders (#870, affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#149) are deployed** — this makes unsigned requests fail closed.
- Expiry stays native-side for now (`expires_at` still surfaced; device clock authority felt native-side).
- Direct third-party RP step-up requests are refused by construction — only enrolled executors can prompt. Intended.
- iOS app bump is the queued follow-up (async parse + `trustedIssuers` + `UntrustedIssuer` handling).

title: feat(vta-service): sign the step-up approve-request (spec: proof REQUIRED)
body:
## What

Part of the cross-repo "signed request legs" programme (affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#147, trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#166): the `auth/step-up/approve-request` spec marks the request proof REQUIRED, and this repo deliberately minted it unsigned. That decision is reversed — the reason prose the human reads must be attributable, and the signed request is retainable evidence; the challenge binding still carries the decision's freshness.

- `mint_pending_step_up` signs the complete document (`eddsa-jcs-2022`, `assertionMethod`) with the `{vta_did}#key-0` issuer secret via `load_vta_issuer_secret(state, vta_did, "step-up")` — the exact `consent_request.rs` pattern, so issuer DID == proof `verificationMethod` DID by construction. Sign failure → internal-error reject: **it never emits unsigned** (fail closed).
- All three gate surfaces load the secret: trust-task `require_step_up`, policy-driven `initiate_self_step_up`, and the REST `RequireStepUp` extractor.
- `issuedAt` added to the minted doc (framework SHOULD; the signed evidence gets a timestamp).
- Module docs rewritten in both `step_up.rs` and `consent_request.rs` — the latter's "contrast with step-up, whose approveRequest is deliberately unsigned" paragraph is gone; both request legs are signed now.

## Behavior change

A VTA with no loadable `{vta_did}#key-0` (or unset `vta_did`) now returns internal-error instead of an unsigned approve-request. Correct per spec; release-note-worthy for unusual key setups.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p vta-service --no-fail-fast` all green: 726 lib + every integration target (`api_integration` 120, `step_up_approve_response` 5, `step_up_policy` 7, `setup` 64); 4 pre-existing ignored
- Unit tests sign with a did:key issuer and cryptographically verify the proof end-to-end (`di_proof::verify_trust_task_proof`), asserting signer == issuer and that the proof covers `payload.ext`
- Gate-path integration tests moved to the provisionable signing app and assert the carried `approveRequest.proof`
- fmt + clippy clean

## Merge notes

- Receivers tolerate the added `proof` (mobile's `parse_step_up_request` ignores unknown members) — safe to merge/deploy before the approver-side enforcement PRs (vta-mobile-core, browser plugin), which must come after.
- Type stays `approve-request/0.1`; the 0.1→0.2 migration is a separate coordinated pass (inbound canonical-URI router + mobile's typed parse move together).

body:
## What

Part of the cross-repo "signed request legs" programme (see affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#147): every approval request leg an approver renders is signed by its issuer, and approvers verify before prompting. This PR is the shared foundation:

1. **`trust-tasks-proof` 0.2.2: a sign-side helper.** `affinidi::sign_trust_task(doc, signer, options)` signs a Trust Task document exactly the way the stock `Verifier` verifies it (doc minus `proof`, in-band `issuer` pre-flighted against the signer key's DID, so output verifies by construction). Defaults: `eddsa-jcs-2022` (deliberately overriding the signer's declared default so the wire suite doesn't vary by signer implementation) and `assertionMethod`. An existing `proof` is replaced, never stacked. Rides the existing `affinidi` feature — no new deps, defaults unchanged. Ends the hand-rolled-signing drift across producers (vta-service today, did-hosting-control next).
2. **Spec clarification, `auth/step-up/approve-request/0.2`:** consumer rule 1 now requires the DID resolved from the proof's `verificationMethod` to equal the document's `issuer` (ported from approve-response/0.2's rule; mismatch → framework `proofInvalid`). No `proofRequirement` front matter touched anywhere.
3. Non-normative signing-profile notes on `task-consent/request/0.1` and `approve-request/0.2` (reference ecosystem signs eddsa-jcs-2022 / assertionMethod; §4.7 keeps the suite open).

## Tests

- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-proof`: 17 pass (8 new sign→stock-verify round-trips: did:key, purpose override, RDFC-with-@context, JCS default vs RDFC-declaring signer, replace semantics, issuer-mismatch/missing-issuer/non-object rejections)
- fmt + clippy `-D warnings` clean; `npm run validate`: 257 specs validated

## Merge notes

- Merge this before the downstream producer PRs so they can migrate their `// TODO: switch to sign_trust_task` hand-rolls after the 0.2.2 release.
- Related but not included: the in-flight `consolidate/*` branches (task-consent `payload.note`, `granted/0.1`) are now a hard dependency of the webvh producer — its signed payload carries `note`, which is only schema-conformant once those land.

title: feat(proof): sign_trust_task helper + approve-request proof-key binding (#166)
body:
feat(proof): sign_trust_task helper + approve-request proof-key binding (#166)

* feat(proof): sign_trust_task — sign-side helper matching the stock verifier's contract

The affinidi backend was verification-only; every producer hand-rolled
DataIntegrityProof::sign + doc["proof"] insertion against an implicit
contract. sign_trust_task makes the contract explicit and symmetric:

- Signs the document with the proof member removed — the identical
  canonicalisation the Verifier applies — and embeds the result.
- Any existing proof is replaced, never nested or appended: re-signing
  means "mint a fresh proof over the current content".
- Pre-flights the SPEC §4.7/§4.8 issuer binding (in-band issuer must
  equal the DID of the signer's verificationMethod), so a document that
  could never verify is refused before a signature is produced.
- Defaults to the reference ecosystem's profile: eddsa-jcs-2022 and
  proofPurpose assertionMethod. The suite default is applied whenever
  SignOptions::cryptosuite is unset — deliberately overriding the
  signer's declared default so the wire suite is deterministic across
  signer implementations.

Rides the existing affinidi feature (same gated deps; a separate sign
feature would gate nothing). Re-exports the upstream Signer trait
(AffinidiSigner), SignOptions, and CryptoSuite so producers need no
direct upstream dep. tests/sign_round_trip.rs proves the loop closed:
documents signed with a did:key secret verify with the crate's own
stock Verifier.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.gore@gmail.com>

* chore(proof): bump trust-tasks-proof to 0.2.2

Patch bump for the sign_trust_task addition — additive API only, and
the crate tracks trust-tasks-rs's MAJOR.MINOR (0.2) per its changelog
convention. No in-repo crate pins trust-tasks-proof, so only the
lockfile moves. Adds the 0.2.2 CHANGELOG entry.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.gore@gmail.com>

* feat(spec): approve-request consumer binds the proof key to the issuer; non-normative signing-profile notes

approve-request/0.2's consumer rules said only "verify the document's
proof" — the response leg already spells out the key-binding half
(verificationMethod DID == document issuer), and without it a verified
signature by *any* key could pass for the named relying party. Port the
approve-response/0.2 rule into the request leg's consumer rule 1,
adapted: the named party here is the relying party, and a mismatch is
the framework proofInvalid error (this task mints no task-specific
code). This is a clarification of the binding SPEC.md §4.7 already
requires — proofRequirement front-matter is untouched, no normative
strengthening or weakening.

Also adds a non-normative note to task-consent/request/0.1 and
approve-request/0.2: the reference ecosystem signs these documents with
eddsa-jcs-2022 / assertionMethod (matching the examples), while §4.7
keeps the cryptosuite choice open. npm run validate passes (257 specs).

title: chore(deps): trust-tasks-rs 0.2.51, messaging SDK 0.18.65 + mediator 0.17.13, acl_set → account_update
body:
Refs OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#854.

Bumps VTI's pinned `trust-tasks-rs` to the consolidation programme's published
output and sweeps every consumer break that follows. What the issue scoped as
one bump plus two list edits turned out to be a **four-link chain**, two links of
which only surfaced under CI.

## The chain

**1. `trust-tasks-rs` 0.2.43 → 0.2.51.** The issue targeted 0.2.50. That is
**not sufficient**, and the failure is silent at compile time — the whole
workspace builds clean at 0.2.50. It fails in #866's new conformance sweep:

```
https://trusttasks.org/spec/acl/list/0.1: response is not canonical:
  unknown field `allowedKeys`, expected one of `approve`, `createdAt`, ...
```

#865 added `allowedKeys` to VTI's ACL entry; the registry published it on
`acl/_shared/0.1/acl-entry` + `acl/update/0.1` one release later, at 0.2.51.
Both those PRs landed while this branch was in flight. 0.2.50 → 0.2.51 changes
nothing else in the workspace's view (identical URI index and module set).

**2. `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.18.62 → 0.18.65 — forced, not chosen.** 0.18.62
does not compile against the bumped registry: it constructs
`messaging::account::list::v0_1::Payload` and
`messaging::access_list::list::v0_1::Payload` with struct-literal syntax, and both
gained optional filter members.

> **Schema-additive is not source-additive.** A new *optional* field is additive to
> the JSON Schema and fully wire-compatible — old producers keep validating, old
> consumers keep parsing. But the generated Rust `struct` carries no
> `#[non_exhaustive]` and no builder, so every downstream crate that constructs the
> payload with a **struct literal** stops compiling: `missing field ...`. The break
> is invisible in the spec diff, invisible on the wire, and surfaces only as a
> downstream build failure one publish-cycle later, in a different repo.

The cheap immunisation is at the *construction* site: end every generated-payload
literal with `..Default::default()` (as `build_allow_all_acl` here does). Whether
the codegen should emit `#[non_exhaustive]` on payload structs — making the
property enforced rather than conventional, at the cost of banning literals — is
worth a decision by the codegen owners. Flagging, not proposing.

**3. `affinidi-messaging-mediator` 0.17.10 → 0.17.13 / `-test-mediator` 0.2.40 →
0.2.43 — the link that only CI could find.** It is a *dev*-dependency, so nothing
in a local `cargo check` touches it. The messaging cutover is clean on **both**
ends: 0.17.10 serves `messaging/acl/set` and answers `account/update/0.1` with

```
WARN  unsupported Trust Task type: https://trusttasks.org/spec/messaging/account/update/0.1
ERROR response failed classification=Status code: 501 Not Implemented
```

So the moment the SDK moves the client side, the embedded test mediator can no
longer provision an ACL at all — the client never gets `receive_forwarded`, and
every forwarded round-trip is refused. The server half ships in 0.17.13.

Stated plainly for deployments: **a mediator older than 0.17.13 cannot serve a VTA
built on messaging SDK 0.18.65.** There is no dual-accept window on either side.

**4. `vta-sdk/src/acl_setup.rs` migrated off the removed `acl_set`.**
affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#668 removed `TrustTasksOps::acl_set` outright. Replacement:

```rust
account_update(profile, did_hash, account_type, acl, queue_limits)
```

on `messaging/account/update/0.1`, which carries `acl` as one optional member
alongside `accountType` / `queueLimits`; `None` for the other two makes it the same
ACL-only partial update. `build_allow_all_acl` now returns
`account::update::v0_1::MediatorAcl` (identical field set). Fire-and-forget
semantics and the deliberate `debug!`-not-`warn!` on timeout are unchanged.

Swept the workspace for the other retired URIs (`account/{change-type,
change-queue-limits}`, `acl/set`, `admin/{add,strip,list,audit-log,config}`,
`access-list/{add,remove,clear,get}`): **no other call site**.

## Publish-lag debt flushed

The shrink-only staleness assertions turn a dependency bump into a forcing
function — these fail CI until removed, which is the harness working as designed:

- **`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs`** — the six `vta/did-templates/*/2.0`
  entries leave `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS` (#851/#864 authored them upstream;
  0.2.49 indexed them). List back to **56**.
- **`vtc-service/tests/trust_task_manifest.rs`** — `vtc/join-requests/decide/`
  leaves `UNPUBLISHED_CANONICAL_OK`, and `spec/vta/` goes **50 → 44** with the
  publish-lag sentence trimmed from its reason string.
- **`docs/05-design-notes/registry-drift-triage.md`** — records the rule this
  produced: *a publish-lag entry is debt with an expiry date, so every
  `trust-tasks-rs` bump is also an exception-list sweep.*

## Reconciliation the bump forces on #866

Indexing the six did-templates 2.0 URIs puts them back inside the conformance
sweep's **derived** census, whose coverage assertion then demands a witness for
each — exactly the hand-off #866 left in a comment. All six are now `checked!`
entries built from the slice's real wire types, and all six conform on the first
run (no `KnownDrift` needed). Each witness carries the **context** form; the
**global** form (`contextId` omitted) is asserted alongside, since the family's
whole point is that scope moved into one optional member — otherwise "optional"
would be the one thing about it the sweep never checks.

`allowedKeys` also enters the three witnesses whose comments promised it would "at
the bump that publishes the member". Worth separating from the exception lists:
**nothing asserted those comments.** A comment claiming a member is unpublished
cannot fail when it stops being true, and this one was stale by one patch release.
The design note records the corollary — a bump's sweep must also grep the pinned
crate for members that comments claim are missing.

## Test evidence

```
cargo test -p vtc-service --test trust_task_manifest   7 passed;   0 failed
cargo test -p vta-service --lib                      726 passed;   0 failed
cargo test -p vta-sdk --lib                          224 passed;   0 failed
cargo check --workspace --all-targets                Finished, no errors
cargo test -p vti-e2e-tests --test client_didcomm      42 passed;   0 failed
cargo fmt --all -- --check                           clean
cargo clippy -p vta-sdk -p vta-service -p vtc-service --all-targets   clean
scripts/check-changelogs.sh / check-version-bumps.sh  both pass
```

The e2e suite is included deliberately: it is the only one that exercises a real
mediator, and it is what proved link 3. It was **21 passed / 21 failed** before —
red on unmodified `main` since #861, independently of this branch, and fixed by
#868. This branch is rebased on #868 and the suite is fully green.

## Releases

`vta-sdk 0.20.25` / `vta-service 0.13.16` / `vtc-service 0.11.44`, root CHANGELOG
entry under `## Unreleased`. Version bumps may be rebased by the orchestrator as
sibling consolidation PRs merge — these slots were consumed out from under this
branch three times already (#864, #865, #866).

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] `account_update(profile, Some(did_hash), None, Some(acl), None)` is the right
      translation of `acl_set(profile, did_hash, acl)` — confirm `None` for
      `account_type` / `queue_limits` means *unchanged* mediator-side. Note one real
      semantic difference found while reading 0.17.13: `account_update` requires the
      account to exist (`account_get` → 404 otherwise), where `acl_set` upserted via
      `get_did_acl(..).unwrap_or_default()`. The e2e suite covers the connect path
      and is green, but this is the sharpest edge in the migration.
- [ ] `account::update::v0_1::MediatorAcl` field set matches the old
      `acl::set::v0_1::MediatorAcl` — no capability silently dropped from the
      allow-all ACL.
- [ ] The mediator floor (≥ 0.17.13) is acceptable for every deployment target, and
      wants saying somewhere operator-facing beyond the CHANGELOG.
- [ ] The six new did-templates witnesses assert the response the handler *actually*
      emits, not the one the spec suggests.
- [ ] `spec/vta/` = 44 and `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS` = 56 are the correct
      post-bump resting state (assertions pass, but the *numbers* are the artifact).

title: fix(e2e): mock the Trust Task envelope the SDK now sends — unblocks a red main (#861)
body:
## main is red, and has been for four merges

The `Test` job on `main` fails with **21 passed / 21 failed** in
`tests/e2e/tests/client_didcomm.rs`. Every failure is the same:

```
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: NotFound("no handler")
```

Confirmed red at 66295b7f (#862), f6257a5f (#863) and c314ae5a (#864); a clean
checkout of unmodified `main` reproduces it, so no open PR is responsible.

## What broke it

#861 (closing #829) routed **every trust-task-twinned `VtaClient` method** off
its legacy `*_management` DIDComm protocol message onto `rpc_tt`. `rpc_tt`'s
DIDComm leg sends the Trust Tasks binding envelope —

```
msg_type: https://trusttasks.org/binding/didcomm/0.1/envelope
body:     { "id": "urn:uuid:…", "type": "<task URI>", "payload": { … } }
```

— so the operation is now identified by the **inner** `type` URI, not by the
message type. The e2e mock VTA (`TestVtaResponder`) still matched only the
legacy message-type constants, so all ~32 migrated methods fell straight
through to the handler's `no handler` branch. The SDK change is correct; only
the mocks were left behind.

Nothing shipped to users was affected — this is a test-fixture gap, which is
exactly why it survived review of #861.

## What this PR changes

`tests/e2e/tests/client_didcomm.rs` only. The responder handlers for the
migrated surfaces now dispatch on the task URI, taking the
`vta_sdk::trust_tasks::TASK_*` constants as the source of truth, and reply with
a trust-task response document (`{ id, type: "<uri>#response", payload }`)
under the envelope message type — which is what `send_and_wait` type-checks the
reply against.

Two small helpers, `is_tt()` and `tt_ok()`, replace the ad-hoc envelope
matching `list_did_templates_via_didcomm` had grown, so there is one spelling
of the shape instead of one per test.

Surfaces now matched on the trust-task URI:

| surface | task URI |
| --- | --- |
| `capabilities` | `spec/vta/discovery/capabilities/1.0` |
| `restart` | `spec/vta/management/reload-services/1.0` |
| `get_config` | `spec/config/show/0.1` |
| `list_keys` / `get_key` / `create_key` / `rename_key` / `invalidate_key` / `sign` | `spec/vta/keys/{list,get,create,rename,revoke,sign}/1.0` |
| `get_key_secret` | `spec/vta/seeds/export-mnemonic/1.0` |
| `list_seeds` / `rotate_seed` | `spec/vta/seeds/{list,rotate}/1.0` |
| `create_acl` / `delete_acl` | `spec/acl/{grant,revoke}/0.1` |
| `list_contexts` / `create_context` / `delete_context` | `spec/vta/contexts/{list,create,delete}/1.0` |
| `get_audit_retention` | `spec/audit/get-retention/1.0` |
| `list_dids_webvh` / `delete_did_webvh` | `spec/vta/webvh/dids/{list,delete}/1.0` |

The surfaces #861 **deliberately did not** migrate keep their legacy
message-type mocks, each with the reason recorded inline: `import_key` and
`backup_export` (twinless), `list_acl` / `update_acl` / `change_acl_role`
(twin request or response shape is not canonical). Those tests are unchanged
apart from the shared `no_handler()` helper.

Three request-shape assertions moved down one level with the payload
(`body["key_type"]` → `body["payload"]["key_type"]`, and likewise for `sign`'s
base64url check and `delete_context`'s `force`), so they still assert what the
SDK actually puts on the wire.

## Release guards

No publishable crate source is touched — the change is confined to
`tests/e2e/`, whose crate (`vti-e2e-tests`) is `publish = false`, and
`check-version-bumps.sh` excludes `tests/` from "source" by design. Both guards
agree, so **no version bump and no CHANGELOG entry are required**:

```
$ scripts/check-version-bumps.sh origin/main
No publishable-crate source changed vs origin/main — nothing to check.

$ scripts/check-changelogs.sh origin/main
No publishable crate versions changed — nothing to check.
```

## Validation

```
$ cargo test -p vti-e2e-tests --test client_didcomm
test result: ok. 42 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

(before: `FAILED. 21 passed; 21 failed`)

`cargo check --workspace --all-targets` and
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

Rebased onto `main` after #866 merged.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Every task URI in the table matches the constant #861 dispatches — the
      `TASK_*` constants in `vta-sdk/src/trust_tasks.rs` are the source of truth.
- [ ] The four legacy-path tests still match message types, not envelopes
      (`import_key`, `backup_export`, `list_acl`, `update_acl`,
      `change_acl_role`) — if a later PR migrates one of them, its mock moves too.
- [ ] `tt_ok()`'s reply is sent under the envelope message type: `send_and_wait`
      rejects any other `typ`, so a reply typed with the task URI would fail.
- [ ] No production code changed.

Refs #829, #861.

title: fix(conformance): every published task's wire shape conforms to its schema, and a sweep that keeps it that way
body:
Closes https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/issues/856
Closes https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/issues/857

## What this does

**#857 — the schema-conformance sweep.** `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/conformance.rs` asserts, for **every** task the dispatcher binds to a published canonical URI, that a representative request body round-trips through the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs::…::Payload` and the response through `…::Response`. The URI census is derived, never hand-listed: `dispatched_uris()` (macro-generated from the same declarations as the dispatch match arms — vta-service's equivalent of the `vtc-service/tests/trust_task_manifest.rs` source scan) filtered to what `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index::schema_for` resolves. That is **63 URIs** under the default feature set.

Two assertions:
- **Coverage** (`every_published_dispatched_uri_has_a_witness`): witness table ⇄ derived census must agree exactly, both directions.
- **Correctness** (`every_witnessed_task_round_trips_through_its_generated_types`): the good case parses, and — per the issue's non-vacuity requirement — every witness is then drifted (unknown member injected) and the drifted form must be **rejected**, so a witness cannot pass against a schema that accepts anything.

An annotated `KnownDrift` allowlist mechanism exists for structural non-conformance. **It ships empty** — every drift the sweep found is fixed in this PR (below), so there are no follow-up issues from this class today.

**#856 — `acl/update`'s request is canonical.** `UpdateAclBody` keeps its historical Rust field names and maps them to the canonical wire with serde renames (`did`→`subject`, `allowed_contexts`→`scopes`), nesting the step-up / approve-authority members under the **shared** `StepUp`/`Approve` components #842 already added in `vta_sdk::protocols::acl_management::entry` (no second definitions). The previously-uncarried `expiresAt` (RFC 3339 on the wire, epoch in the store) and `reason` (recorded via `audit::record_with_detail`) members are now carried. The comment-only pin in `trust_tasks/acl.rs` (#855) is a real assertion: full round-trip through `specs::acl::update::v0_1::Payload`, plus a teeth check that reintroduces the pre-fix `did` spelling and requires rejection.

## What the sweep caught (all fixed here, not allowlisted)

The first full run found eight more non-conformances beyond #856's known one. All were the trivial class (wire spelling / missing-or-extra members with the data already in hand), so per the stream instruction they are fixed in this PR:

| Task | Drift | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `acl/list` response | legacy bare `Vec<CreateAclResultBody>` (snake_case rows) | handler now uses the existing canonical wrapper `operations::acl::list_entries` |
| `acl/show` response | legacy flat row | handler now uses `operations::acl::show_by_subject` |
| `acl/change-role` response | bare flat row | wrapped in canonical `{entry}` (`CreateAclResponseBody`) |
| `acl/swap-key` response | bare flat row; `previousSubject` missing | new `SwapKeyResultBody {entry, previousSubject}` |
| `auth/revoke-session` response | empty `{}`; schema requires `revokedCount` | field added (vta-mobile-core already parsed `revokedCount` — the SDK type was the outlier) |
| `device/wipe` response | `wipedAt`/`disabledAt`/`reason` not in the closed schema; `completedAt` missing | emits canonical `{deviceId, scope, completedAt}` |
| `vault/proxy-login` response | cleartext `sessionId`/`expiresAt` at the root of a closed object | moved under vendor-namespaced `ext` (`org.openvtc.vault-session`, following the step-up slice's `org.openvtc.*` convention) |
| `provision/integration` request+response | snake_case / kebab-case emission vs the canonical 0.2 camelCase (`ProvisionSummary`, `AssertionMode`, `vcValiditySeconds`, `createContext`) | emission flipped to camelCase; snake/kebab kept as intake aliases. This reverses #517's "emit conservative" direction deliberately: 0.2 is now the **only** URI the dispatcher binds, and its schema is `additionalProperties: false` |
| `vta/webvh/dids/update` response | snake_case emission (`new_version_id`, …) | `UpdateDidWebvhResultBody` emits camelCase per its published schema; snake aliases kept on intake |

Also fixed in passing: the SDK client's legacy-DIDComm `update_acl` body already sent `subject` (so it could never have matched the old `did` field — that path was already non-functional); its remaining `allowed_contexts` key moves to the canonical `scopes`.

## Scope notes

- The sweep lives in vta-service because that is where the dispatch table (and its macro-generated census) lives. Extending the same pattern to vtc-service's REST-bound tasks is possible but is a separate ~60-URI witness effort against axum route types; not attempted here.
- 0.1↔0.2 dual-accept URIs: `wire_v0_2` edge-transformed 0.2 URIs are not dispatch arms (they are down-converted before dispatch) and keep their own transform tests; the genuinely dual-dispatched `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.1|0.2` has one witness per version with version-distinct `evidence.kind` fixtures.
- Pre-production wire changes (device/wipe, proxy-login, provision, dids/update) are clean canonical fixes rather than compatibility shims, per the programme's direction; intake keeps accepting the legacy spellings via serde aliases wherever a legacy producer could exist.

## Rebase expectation

~8 sibling consolidation streams are currently rebinding URIs. As they merge, the sweep's derived census will change and its **coverage assertion will fail asking for new witnesses — that is the check doing its job**, not a defect of this PR. This already happened once during development: the branch is rebased over #858–#862, and #860's constant-rename pass surfaced immediately in the sweep table (absorbed here) — exactly the behaviour the check exists for. Version bumps / CHANGELOG placement may need the same trivial rebase again as more siblings merge (currently vta-sdk 0.20.19 → **0.20.20**, vta-service 0.13.11 → **0.13.12**).

## Validation

- `cargo test -p vta-service` — full suite green (includes the two sweep tests over 63 URIs and the un-pinned #856 assertion).
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk` — green.
- `cargo test -p vta-mobile-core -p pnm-cli -p cnm-cli -p vta-webvh -p vta-cli-common` — green; `cargo check --tests` green for every vta-sdk dependent crate.
- Local dry-runs of the CI release guards pass: version-bump guard, changelog guard, lockfile self-pins.
- `cargo fmt` clean on touched crates.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] `conformance.rs`: the witness table's fixtures faithfully mirror the handlers whose local types are module-private (consent, task-consent, vault) — each is annotated with the type it mirrors.
- [ ] The wire changes in the table above are acceptable as clean fixes (no compatibility shim) given pre-production status; intake aliases retained where a legacy producer could exist.
- [ ] `vault/proxy-login`: agreement that `ext["org.openvtc.vault-session"]` is the right home for the cleartext session hints.
- [ ] `UpdateAclParams` gained `expires_at`/`reason`; REST `PATCH /acl/{did}` deliberately does not carry them (its own body is unchanged).

title: No check that a canonically-bound task's payload conforms to its published schema
body:
## Problem

Nothing checks that a task bound to a **published** canonical URI actually conforms to that URI's schema. We have two parity checks today and this is the missing third:

| Check | Exists? | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Every SDK constant is dispatched | yes | routing |
| Every dispatched URI has a registry spec | proposed in #854 | coverage |
| **Every specced URI's payload conforms to its schema** | **no** | correctness |

The gap is not theoretical — it already produced a live defect. `acl/update` has been rejected at the dispatch spine since #842 because its request body emits `did` where the schema requires `subject`. See the companion issue.

## Why it hides

- **Requests** are validated at runtime by `validate_payload`, but only on the Trust Task transport. REST and the legacy DIDComm messages carry their own bodies, so a non-conformant canonical body is invisible unless someone exercises that one path.
- **Responses are never validated at runtime at all.** Only a test can catch a non-conformant response.
- Folding a task onto a *published* URI silently turns schema validation on. An unpublished `spec/vta/*` URI has no entry in `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index`, so it dispatches unvalidated; repointing the constant enables `additionalProperties: false` and required-field checks on live traffic, with no compile-time signal.

Only three tasks have ever had a conformance test: `config/*` (#841), `audit/list` (#848), `acl/change-role` (#855). Everything else folded in this programme is unverified.

## Proposal

One sweep test asserting, for every canonically-bound task, that a representative request body deserializes into its generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs::…::Payload`, and the response body into `…::Response`. The generated types carry `deny_unknown_fields` plus the spec's required set, so the round-trip *is* the conformance check:

```rust
let json = serde_json::to_value(&our_body)?;
serde_json::from_value::<canonical::Payload>(json.clone())
    .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("not canonical: {e}\n{json:#}"));
```

**Write it so it cannot pass vacuously.** The `acl/update` defect went unnoticed across three PRs because an assertion of the form "adding a forbidden member makes this fail" passed while the body was *already* failing for an unrelated reason. Assert the good case parses, then prove the check has teeth by drifting a member and asserting rejection.

## Scope

Candidates are every URI under `https://trusttasks.org/spec/` that `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index::schema_for` resolves — the same set `vtc-service/tests/trust_task_manifest.rs` already enumerates for the census, so the list can be derived rather than hand-maintained.

Worth running before further work on the fold programme (docs/05-design-notes/canonical-task-reduction.md, phases C–E), since it either clears what has already shipped or finds the rest of this class in one pass.

## Related

- #854 — registry↔implementation drift in the opposite direction (implemented URIs with no spec).
- #840 — the fold programme that produced the bindings this would check.

title: acl/update is rejected at the dispatch spine: its request body is not canonical (subject vs did)
body:
## Problem

`acl/update`'s **request** body is not canonical. It emits `did`/`allowedContexts` where `acl/update/0.1` requires `subject`/`scopes`, and it has no nested `stepUp`/`approve` objects:

```
unknown field `did`, expected one of `approve`, `expiresAt`, `ext`,
`label`, `reason`, `scopes`, `stepUp`, `subject`
```

Because `spec/acl/update/0.1` **is** published, `trust_tasks/mod.rs::validate_payload` finds a schema for it and validates against it. A conforming `acl/update` document is therefore rejected at the dispatch spine with `malformed_request`.

## Why nothing caught it

The other two transports carry their own bodies, so neither exercises the canonical shape:

- **REST** `PATCH /acl/{did}` binds its own `UpdateAclRequest` (`routes/acl.rs`).
- **DIDComm** uses the legacy `firstperson.network/protocols/acl-management/1.0/update-acl` message, which has no schema and so is never validated.

Only the **Trust Task** transport hits the canonical schema, and it had no test.

## Origin

#842 folded the ACL family onto canonical `acl/*`. It made the *response* canonical — via the shared `AclEntry` component plus a compatibility layer on the client types — and repointed the URI, but left the request shape as it was.

## Fix

Give `UpdateAclBody` the same compatibility-layer treatment #842 gave the response: keep the historical Rust field names, map them to the canonical wire with serde renames.

| Rust field | Canonical wire |
|---|---|
| `did` | `subject` |
| `allowed_contexts` | `scopes` |
| `step_up_approver`, `step_up_require` | nested `stepUp` object |
| `approve_scope` | nested `approve` object |
| — | `expiresAt`, `reason` (not currently carried) |

The nested `stepUp`/`approve` shapes already exist as canonical components in `vta_sdk::protocols::acl_management::entry`, added by #842 for the response — reuse them rather than defining second versions.

Verify by round-tripping the serialized body through `trust_tasks_rs::specs::acl::update::v0_1::Payload`, which carries `deny_unknown_fields` and the spec's required set.

## Notes

- Currently pinned by a comment in `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/acl.rs` tests (added in #855) so it cannot be mistaken for conformant, but **not asserted** — the test would fail for this unrelated reason.
- Found in #855 only because a conformance assertion was passing for the *wrong* reason; see #857 for the systemic version.
- Related but distinct from #854, which covers the opposite direction (implemented URIs with **no** registry spec). This one is a URI that *has* a spec and does not conform to it.

title: fix(conformance): every published task's wire shape conforms to its schema, and a sweep that keeps it that way (#866)
body:
fix(conformance): every published task's wire shape conforms to its schema, and a sweep that keeps it that way (#866)

* fix(acl): make acl/update's request body canonical (subject/scopes, nested stepUp/approve)

acl/update has been rejected at the dispatch spine since #842 repointed
the URI onto the published spec: repointing switched schema validation
on while the body still emitted did/allowedContexts where acl/update/0.1
requires subject/scopes, with no nested stepUp/approve objects.

Give UpdateAclBody the compatibility-layer treatment #842 gave the
response: historical Rust field names, canonical wire via serde renames,
reusing the shared StepUp/Approve components from
vta_sdk::protocols::acl_management::entry rather than defining second
versions. Also carry the spec's expiresAt (RFC 3339 on the wire, epoch
in the store) and reason (recorded with the audit entry) members, which
the body previously dropped.

The comment-only pin in vta-service trust_tasks/acl.rs (#855) becomes a
real assertion: a fully-populated body round-trips through the generated
trust_tasks_rs::specs::acl::update::v0_1::Payload, and the check is
proven non-vacuous by reintroducing the pre-fix spelling and requiring
rejection.

The SDK client's legacy-DIDComm update body already sent subject (so
that path was already non-functional against the old field names); its
remaining allowed_contexts key moves to the canonical scopes.

Closes #856

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(conformance): sweep every published task's wire shape against its schema

Nothing checked that a task bound to a PUBLISHED canonical URI actually
speaks that URI's schema. Folding a task onto a published URI silently
turns validate_payload on at the dispatch spine, so a non-canonical body
then fails on live traffic with no compile-time signal — which is how
acl/update shipped broken (#856, via #842).

trust_tasks/conformance.rs closes that. The URI census is derived, never
hand-listed: dispatched_uris() (macro-generated from the same
declarations as the dispatch match arms) intersected with what
trust_tasks_rs::schema_index::schema_for resolves — 63 URIs today. Two
assertions: coverage (witness table and derived census agree exactly,
both directions) and correctness (request parses as the generated
Payload, response as the generated Response). Per #857, non-vacuity is
mechanical rather than a matter of care: after the good case passes,
every witness is drifted with an unknown member and the drifted form
MUST be rejected, so a witness cannot pass against a schema that accepts
anything.

The first full run found eight non-conformances beyond the known
acl/update one. All were the wire-spelling class, so all are fixed here
and the KnownDrift allowlist ships empty:

- acl/list, acl/show responses: the trust-task handlers returned legacy
  flat rows; they now use the canonical list_entries / show_by_subject
  wrappers that already existed beside them.
- acl/change-role, acl/swap-key responses: wrapped in the canonical
  {entry} / {entry, previousSubject} (new SwapKeyResultBody).
- auth/revoke-session response: carries the required revokedCount. It
  was an empty object — vta-mobile-core already parsed the count, so the
  SDK type was the outlier, not the consumer.
- device/wipe response: canonical {deviceId, scope, completedAt}. The
  schema is closed and wipedAt/disabledAt/reason are not in it; the
  disable side-effect is unchanged and still asserted via list filters.
- vault/proxy-login response: the cleartext sessionId/expiresAt hints
  move under ext["org.openvtc.vault-session"], following the step-up
  slice's convention — the canonical response object is closed.
- provision/integration: emission flips to the canonical 0.2
  lowerCamelCase (ProvisionSummary, AssertionMode, vcValiditySeconds,
  createContext), with snake/kebab retained as intake aliases. This
  deliberately reverses #517's direction: 0.2 is now the only URI the
  dispatcher binds. request_body_for_version/response_body_for_version
  invert accordingly — 0.2 is the identity, 0.1 is the down-cast.
- vta/webvh/dids/update response: UpdateDidWebvhResultBody emits
  camelCase per its published schema, snake aliases kept on intake; the
  REST integration assertions move with it.

Closes #857

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(conformance): invert the provision-integration recase helpers with their emission

The 0.2-camelCase emission flip left the helper unit test naming the old
snake->camel functions, so the vta-sdk lib test target no longer built.
Rename with the direction they now run (camel -> snake/kebab, since the
types serialise the canonical 0.2 form and 0.1 is the down-cast), and
restore the #[allow(deprecated)] on the witness table for the same
reason the dispatch table carries it: the deprecated 0.1 constants are
still dispatched during the migration window, so they are still in the
census the table must cover.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(conformance): record the stale-witness direction, which #864 exercised

Both directions of the coverage assertion matter and only one of them is
obvious. A dispatched URI with no witness is the case the check was
written for; a witness for a URI nothing dispatches any more is equally
drift, and it is the direction that tells you a fold has landed. #864
fired exactly that, so say so where the next reader will hit it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: docs(contributing): a patch bump promises wire compatibility, not Rust source compatibility
body:
## The problem

Adding an optional member to an existing payload is additive **on the wire** — which is why the contributing guide calls it a patch bump — but it is source-breaking for generated Rust consumers, because `trust-tasks-rs` emits plain structs with public fields and any struct-literal construction stops compiling.

It has bitten twice in the last week:

1. **`affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.18.62** stopped compiling against `trust-tasks-rs` 0.2.50 when `messaging/account/list` and `messaging/access-list/list` gained optional filters (#158). Bumping the SDK to 0.18.65 then cascaded into a further consumer break, which is what OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#867 is cleaning up.
2. **This repo's own binding examples and end-to-end tests** (`trust-tasks-https`, `trust-tasks-didcomm`) stopped compiling when `AclEntry` gained `allowedKeys` (#164) — caught by the full-workspace `cargo test` job.

Neither is dangerous — a compile error is a good failure mode — but both landed on consumers who had only bumped a patch version, and neither was anticipated by the guide.

## What this PR does

Documents the property in `CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md` next to the existing patch/minor rule: what breaks, who it lands on, that authors should flag it in the changelog entry, and that consumers should construct payloads by deserialization (`serde_json::from_value`) rather than struct literals. Docs only — no schema, binding, or version changes.

## Why not fix it in the codegen

I tried, and it does not work:

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| `TypeSpaceSettings::with_derive("Default")` so consumers could write `..Default::default()` | **480 compile errors** — `#[derive(Default)]` on generated enums with no `#[default]` variant |
| Narrowing the derive to structs only (2474 sites) | **323 errors** — those structs embed the same enums |
| Giving each generated enum a default variant | Rejected as unsafe: it would let a `decision` enum default to `approved`. A compile error is strictly better than a silently-defaulted security-relevant value |
| `with_struct_builder(true)` | Would work, but replaces the construction API for every consumer at once — a much larger change than the problem warrants, and worth its own discussion if the ecosystem ever wants it |

Recording the negative result here so the next person does not repeat it.

## Note on the versioning scheme

The libraries' `MAJOR.MINOR` tracks the SPEC framework version, so there is no free minor bump available to signal a Rust-source break in the way Cargo's semver conventions would normally expect. That constraint is the reason this is documentation rather than a version-policy change — flagging it in case editors want to revisit the coupling separately.
