title: feat(acl): allowedKeys — scope a caller to specific signing-oracle keys (#818)
body:
Closes #818

Spec sibling: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#164 (`AclEntry.allowedKeys` on the canonical `acl/_shared/0.1/acl-entry` component + `acl/update/0.1` prose).

## The gap

The **resource** dimension of an ACL grant was expressible only as a *context*. `Capability::Sign` is unparameterized, so "this caller may invoke the signing oracle on exactly key K" could not be said — the only spelling was giving K a context of its own, forcing context topology to encode per-key authorization. `ContextPolicy.signable_keys` is not the answer: it is **resource-bound by design** (it constrains the key's context for *every* actor, super-admin included — the property that lets a VTC- or fleet-pushed policy bind every signer). This adds the actor-scoped half; the two are complementary.

## The field (`vti-common`)

```rust
pub allowed_keys: Option<BTreeSet<String>>,   // #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
```

The effective decision is **never** read off the raw `Option`. It decodes once through `key_scope_for` / `AclEntry::key_scope()` into

```rust
enum KeyScope { AllInScope, Keys(BTreeSet<String>) }   // ask KeyScope::allows(key_id)
```

— the same shape `ActScope` gave the context axis. `None` → `AllInScope` (every key the entry's contexts reach); `Some(set)` → `Keys(set)` **including the empty set**, which authorizes no keys. That is issue trap 1: `docs/05-design-notes/acl-scope-semantics.md` records three defects (#746, #770, #769) from testing `allowed_contexts.is_empty()` at a call site, and this member has the same empty-vs-absent hazard. There is no `is_empty()` on the key axis anywhere in the diff.

Additive and fail-closed: `#[serde(default)]` means every existing row deserialises to `None` and behaves byte-identically.

## The gate (`vta-service`)

Gate 4 in `operations::keys::sign_payload`, placed deliberately:

- **After `auth.require_context(ctx)`** — as the issue specifies. The filter intersects with the context scope and can only narrow, so a caller naming a key outside its contexts is refused by gate 1 before its own filter is even consulted. Pinned by `sign_payload_allowed_keys_only_narrows_never_widens`.
- **Before the policy quota** — a refused call burns none of the context's daily sign budget.
- **On the unscoped-key path too** — a super-admin whose row carries a filter asked to be bound by it.

All three transports (REST, DIDComm `key-management/1.0/sign-request`, `keys/sign` Trust Task) funnel through this one function, so this is one edit, not three. `sign_payload` gains an `acl_ks` parameter; the three call sites are updated.

The gate reads the **stored ACL row**, not the JWT. That is deliberate and is also the answer to **trap 3** (see below): narrowing an entry's filter binds the subject's *next* sign request, with no session revocation and no access-token-TTL window.

## Wire plumbing (`vta-sdk` + handlers) — trap 2

`CreateAclBody` is the exact struct family where a camelCase/snake_case mismatch once let an empty `allowed_contexts` silently mint a super-admin (#656/#658), so the spelling is pinned by tests at every layer:

- canonical wire `AclEntry.allowedKeys: Option<Vec<String>>`, skipped on **`is_none`, never `is_empty`** — `"allowedKeys": []` must survive the wire or the narrowest grant becomes the widest (`allowed_keys_empty_and_absent_both_survive_the_wire`);
- `UpdateAclBody.allowed_keys: Option<Option<Vec<String>>>` with a `double_option` deserializer and `rename = "allowedKeys"`, so **omitted / explicit `null` / array** stay three distinct intentions (`allowed_keys_round_trips_as_camel_case`, `allowed_keys_distinguishes_absent_null_and_empty`, `allowed_keys_clear_serializes_as_explicit_null`);
- same three-way shape on the REST `PATCH /acl/{did}` body and on `vta_sdk::client::UpdateAclRequest` (`test_update_acl_request_allowed_keys_three_intentions`).

Wired through REST `POST /acl` + `PATCH /acl/{did}`, DIDComm `create-acl`/`update-acl`, the `acl/grant` + `acl/update` Trust Tasks, `CreateAclRequest::allowed_keys(..)`, and every grant/show/list/update echo. Empty-string key ids are refused at create and update (the `--contexts ''` lesson one axis over).

## CLI + docs

- `pnm|cnm acl create --allowed-keys <ids>`;
- `pnm|cnm acl update --allowed-keys <ids>` or `--allowed-keys-unrestricted` to remove the filter. Clearing gets its own flag for the same reason `--approve-none` does: an empty `--allowed-keys` cannot mean both "no keys at all" and "no filter".
- Displays render the empty filter as `(none — may invoke the signing oracle on no keys)`, never blank and never "unrestricted" — the #746 lesson.
- `docs/02-vta/integration-guide.md` §"What authorizes a sign request" is now **four** gates, and the per-context granularity callout points at `--allowed-keys` for the one-key-out-of-a-shared-context case.

## Trap 3 — revocation semantics (a finding, not a code change)

`is_privilege_reduction` does **not** need to account for `allowedKeys`:

- it lives in `vtc-service/src/routes/acl.rs` and is VTC-only; the VTC runs no signing oracle and `VtcAclEntry` has no `allowed_keys` to narrow;
- its purpose is to revoke sessions when authority that rides in the **JWT claims** (role, contexts) shrinks. `allowed_keys` never enters the claims — gate 4 reads the stored row on every request, so a narrowing is effective immediately. That is strictly stronger than session revocation, and it avoids logging every subject out over a per-key tweak.

Worth a reviewer's confirmation, since the alternative (mirroring the field into claims and revoking on narrowing) is defensible but buys nothing here.

## Validation

```
cargo test -p vta-service      → 719 + 120 + 64 + … all suites ok, 0 failed
cargo test -p vti-common       → ok (incl. 4 new KeyScope / serde tests)
cargo test -p vta-sdk          → 376 + 359 + … ok (incl. 4 new wire tests)
cargo test -p vta-cli-common   → ok (incl. 2 new display/flag tests)
cargo clippy -p vti-common -p vta-sdk -p vta-service -p vta-cli-common -p pnm-cli -p cnm-cli --all-targets → 0 errors, 0 warnings
cargo check --workspace --all-targets → clean
cargo fmt --all → clean
```

New tests: `sign_payload_honours_acl_allowed_keys`, `sign_payload_allowed_keys_only_narrows_never_widens`, `update_acl_sets_empties_and_clears_the_key_filter`, `key_scope_*`, `legacy_row_without_allowed_keys_deserialises_to_none`, `empty_allowed_keys_survives_serde_round_trip`, plus the wire/casing tests listed above.

## Release housekeeping

`vti-common` 0.11.30, `vta-sdk` 0.20.17, **`vta-service` 0.13.10** (0.13.9 is claimed by the in-flight #858), `vta-cli-common` 0.10.21, `pnm-cli` 0.11.15, `cnm-cli` 0.11.12, with a root `CHANGELOG.md` entry under Unreleased.

## Coordination

A sibling stream is fixing **#856** (`UpdateAclBody` canonical field renames) in these same `acl_management` files. This branch is based on `origin/main` as-is and its diff is deliberately additive — **a small rebase against the #856 fix is expected**. The one member this PR adds is already spelled canonically (`allowedKeys`), so it should survive that rename untouched.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Gate 4 sits after `require_context` and cannot widen — confirm `sign_payload_allowed_keys_only_narrows_never_widens` pins what you'd expect.
- [ ] No bare `is_empty()` on the key axis; `Some(∅)` really does refuse every key (`sign_payload_honours_acl_allowed_keys`, final block).
- [ ] The three-way update semantics (omitted / `null` / `[]`) are right for a maintainer's mental model, and the wire casing is pinned everywhere it is carried.
- [ ] The trap-3 finding — leaving `is_privilege_reduction` alone because the gate reads the live row — is the call you'd make.

title: ACL grants cannot scope a caller to specific key ids (only to a whole context)
body:
Split out of the design review in #817 (`docs/05-design-notes/multi-tenant-signing.md`, R2). Stands on its own merits — this is a least-privilege gap independent of the Cierge deployment that surfaced it.

## The gap

The **resource** dimension of an ACL grant is expressible only as a *context*.

`AclEntry.capabilities` is a flat `Vec<Capability>`, and `Capability::Sign` is unparameterized (`vti-common/src/acl/mod.rs:122-145`). So this cannot be said:

> this caller may invoke the signing oracle on **exactly key K**

The only way to scope a caller to one key today is to give that key **a context of its own**. That works — it is what the design note recommends for multi-tenant signers — but it forces context topology to encode per-key authorization, which is a different concern. Any consumer that legitimately needs one key out of a shared context must be handed the whole context.

## Why `signable_keys` is not the answer

`ContextPolicy.signable_keys` (`vta-sdk/src/context_policy.rs:48-50`) already restricts which key ids the signing oracle may be invoked on — but it is **resource-bound by design**: it constrains the key's context for *every* actor uniformly, including super-admin. That property is load-bearing (it is what lets a VTC- or fleet-pushed policy bind every signer, relaxable only through policy CRUD).

It therefore cannot express "*this caller*, this key". The two mechanisms are complementary, not substitutes — this issue asks for the actor-scoped half.

## Proposal

An optional actor-scoped key filter on the ACL entry, **intersected with** — never widening — the existing context scope:

```rust
/// Key ids this entry may invoke the signing oracle on. `None` = every key
/// in `allowed_contexts` (today's behaviour). Intersects with the context
/// scope; it can only narrow, never widen, so an entry naming a key outside
/// its contexts still cannot use it.
#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
pub allowed_keys: Option<BTreeSet<String>>,
```

Enforced in `operations::keys::sign_payload` as a fourth gate, **after** the existing `auth.require_context(ctx)` (`vta-service/src/operations/keys.rs:840`) so a caller can never reach a key outside its contexts by naming it here.

Additive and fail-closed: `None` on every existing row preserves behaviour byte-identically, the same way `capabilities` was introduced.

## Why a separate field rather than parameterising `Capability::Sign`

`Capability::Sign { keys: … }` would change the shape of a serialized enum that already ships in ACL rows and on the `acl_management` wire. A sibling `Option` field is additive and needs no migration. (Open to the alternative if someone prefers it, but the migration cost looks disproportionate.)

## Scope of the change

- `vti-common/src/acl/mod.rs` — the field, plus an accessor that returns the effective decision rather than exposing the raw `Option` (see the `ActScope` precedent below).
- `vta-service/src/operations/keys.rs` — gate 4 in `sign_payload`. Note all three transports (REST, DIDComm `key-management/1.0/sign-request`, `keys/sign` Trust Task) funnel through that one function, so this is one edit, not three.
- `vta-sdk/src/protocols/acl_management/{create,update}.rs` — wire plumbing.
- `vta-cli-common` — an `--allowed-keys` flag on `acl create` / `acl update`.
- Docs: `docs/02-vta/integration-guide.md` §"What authorizes a sign request" gains gate 4.

## Traps worth stating up front

1. **Do not add a bare `is_empty()` check.** `allowed_contexts` already has the empty-means-two-different-things problem that `ActScope` exists to solve (see `docs/05-design-notes/acl-scope-semantics.md` — it has produced three separate defects: #746, #770, #769). `Some(empty_set)` must mean **authorized on no keys**, not "unrestricted"; `None` means unrestricted. Model it so the distinction cannot be got backwards, and do not test emptiness at call sites.
2. **Casing drift on the wire.** `CreateAclBody` is the exact struct where a camelCase/snake_case mismatch once let an empty `allowed_contexts` silently mint a super-admin (#656/#658). Whatever `allowed_keys` serializes as, pin it with a round-trip test and keep `deny_unknown_fields` behaviour consistent with its siblings.
3. **Revocation semantics.** Narrowing an entry's `allowed_keys` should behave like any other privilege reduction — check whether the existing session-revocation path on reduction (`is_privilege_reduction`) needs to account for it, or a caller keeps the wider set until its access token expires.

## Explicitly out of scope

This does **not** address the threat in #805 — a process that legitimately signs for N identities holds authority for N identities, and no authorization refinement changes that (#817, Finding 2). This is about being able to express least privilege where the split *is* meaningful.

feat(acl): allowedKeys — scope a caller to specific signing-oracle keys (#865)

Closes #818.

An ACL grant's resource dimension was expressible only as a context, so
"this caller may invoke the signing oracle on exactly key K" could not be
said — the only spelling was giving K a context of its own.
ContextPolicy.signable_keys cannot express it either: it is resource-bound
by design, constraining the key's context for every actor uniformly. This
adds the actor-scoped half, mirroring the canonical
acl/_shared/0.1/acl-entry#allowedKeys member (trust-tasks 0.2.45).

The field (vti-common):
- AclEntry.allowed_keys: Option<BTreeSet<String>>, #[serde(default)] —
  every existing row deserialises to None, behaviour byte-identical.
- The effective decision is a KeyScope (AllInScope | Keys(set)) decoded
  once via key_scope_for / AclEntry::key_scope(), the same shape ActScope
  gave the context axis: None = every key in scope, Some(EMPTY) =
  authorized on NO keys. No call site tests emptiness (trap 1 — the
  #746/#769/#770 defect class the ActScope precedent exists for).

The gate (vta-service):
- Gate 4 in operations::keys::sign_payload, strictly AFTER
  auth.require_context(ctx) — the filter intersects with the context
  scope, never widens it; a caller naming a key outside its contexts is
  refused by the context gate first — and BEFORE the policy quota, so a
  refused call burns no daily sign budget. Applies to the unscoped
  (super-admin-only) key path too.
- One enforcement point covers all three transports (REST, DIDComm
  sign-request, keys/sign Trust Task).
- The gate reads the STORED ACL row, not the JWT: narrowing an entry's
  filter binds the subject's next sign request — no session revocation,
  no token-TTL window (trap 3; see below).

Wire plumbing (vta-sdk + handlers):
- Canonical wire AclEntry gains allowedKeys (Option<Vec<String>>,
  skip-if-None so "allowedKeys": [] survives the wire).
- acl/update carries the three-intention replacement as a double-Option:
  omitted = leave unchanged, explicit null = clear (privilege increase),
  empty array = no keys. Wire name pinned to allowedKeys with round-trip
  tests (trap 2 — the #656/#658 casing-drift history), consistent across
  the trust-task body, the REST PATCH body, and the SDK client request.
- Wired through REST POST /acl + PATCH /acl/{did}, DIDComm and Trust Task
  acl/grant + acl/update, CreateAclRequest::allowed_keys(..), and
  grant/show/list/update echoes.
- Empty-string key ids are refused at create and update (the
  --contexts '' lesson one axis over).

CLI (vta-cli-common, pnm-cli, cnm-cli):
- acl create --allowed-keys <ids>; acl update --allowed-keys <ids> |
  --allowed-keys-unrestricted (clearing is its own flag — an empty
  --allowed-keys cannot mean both "no keys" and "no filter").
- Displays render the empty filter as "no keys", never blank or
  unrestricted (#746 lesson).

Docs: integration-guide §"What authorizes a sign request" is now four
gates, and the per-context granularity callout points to --allowed-keys
for the one-key-out-of-a-shared-context case.

change — it is VTC-only, the VTC runs no signing oracle and VtcAclEntry
has no allowed_keys; on the VTA the live store-read makes narrowing

title: feat(acl): AclEntry gains allowedKeys — an actor-scoped signing-key filter
body:
Addresses https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/issues/818

Implementation sibling: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#865.

## What and why

The `acl/*` family can say *where* a subject may act (`scopes`) and *what it may confer* (`approve`), but it has no way to say **which keys** a subject may invoke a maintainer's signing oracle on. The only way to scope a caller to one key is to give that key a scope of its own — which forces scope topology to encode per-key authorization, a different concern. This adds the actor-scoped filter.

## The member

`AclEntry.allowedKeys` (optional array of key-id strings) on the shared `acl/_shared/0.1/acl-entry` component, plus a replacement form on the `acl/update/0.1` payload. Draft-additive, in place.

Semantics, stated identically in the schema, `_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md` §5, and the grant/update prose:

- **Intersects with — never widens — `scopes`.** A key named here that lies outside the entry's scopes remains unreachable, exactly as if it were not named.
- **Absent = every key within the entry's scopes** — the behaviour of every entry that pre-dates the member.
- **Present-but-empty = authorized on NO keys.** The opposite of absent, and deliberately so. Emptiness is never a wildcard; a consumer MUST carry the distinction end to end rather than testing emptiness at a call site. This is the family's existing empty-is-not-unrestricted rule (§5) applied to a new axis.

## `acl/update` — the one narrowing this task carries

`acl/update` otherwise refuses narrowing and routes it to `acl/revoke`. `allowedKeys` is a deliberate exception, because `acl/revoke/0.1`'s reduction vocabulary is `scopes` and cannot express a per-key reduction — refusing it here too would leave the filter tightenable by no task at all.

The exception relocates the doctrine's obligations rather than relaxing them. A narrowing replacement **is a privilege reduction**, and a consumer MUST audit it as one *and* apply it to the subject's live sessions rather than letting the wider set survive until a credential expires. The three intentions of *replacement, not merge* all carry weight: omitted = leave alone, explicit `null` = clear the filter (a privilege **increase**, gate like clearing `expiresAt`), empty array = no keys at all.

## Schema-shape note worth a reviewer's eye

The shared member is typed `["array", "null"]` rather than plain `array`. That is not cosmetic: with a plain array, typify generates `Vec<String>` with `skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty"`, which **collapses absent and empty into one value** — turning the narrowest possible grant into the widest one in every Rust consumer. Nullable forces `Option<Vec<String>>`, so the distinction the prose insists on survives codegen. Explicit `null` on the entry is documented as equivalent to absent (producers SHOULD omit).

## Validation

```
npm run build      → Validated 257 specs, indexed 46 shared schemas. Done.
cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs → all suites ok (294 + 13 + 9 + 7 + 6 + 5 + 3 + 1 passed, 0 failed)
cargo check -p trust-tasks-rs --all-targets → clean
```

Bindings regenerated (`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`, `npm run build-ts-bindings`); `trust-tasks-rs` and `@openvtc/trust-tasks` bumped in lockstep 0.2.44 → 0.2.45 with a CHANGELOG entry and a refreshed `Cargo.lock`. The `AclEntry` struct literals in the hand-written `trust-tasks-rs` tests/examples gained `allowed_keys: None`.

Version bumps / generated bindings may be rebased by the orchestrator as sibling consolidation PRs merge.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Absent / present-but-empty semantics read unambiguously in the schema description, CONVENTIONS §5, and both spec prose sections — and agree with each other.
- [ ] The `["array", "null"]` typing is accepted for the codegen reason above (or you prefer plain `array` + a hand-written binding override).
- [ ] `acl/update` carrying the one narrowing `acl/revoke` cannot express is the right call, and the audit + live-session obligations are stated strongly enough to substitute for routing it through `acl/revoke`.
- [ ] `allowedKeys` belongs on the shared entry (visible to `grant`/`show`/`list`) rather than only on `grant`.

Companion spec PR (must merge and publish first): trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#162 (`vta/did-templates/*/2.0`, trust-tasks-rs 0.2.49 slot).

## Summary

Implements the did-templates consolidation: the global (`vta/did-templates/*/1.0`) and context-scoped (`vta/contexts/did-templates/*/1.0`) trust-task families merge into six `vta/did-templates/*/2.0` URIs. title: Consolidate vta/did-templates/* and vta/contexts/did-templates/* into one six-task family
body:
## Proposal

Collapse the twelve-task pair of spec families `vta/did-templates/{create,delete,get,list,render,update}/1.0` and `vta/contexts/did-templates/{same six}/1.0` into **one six-task family** with an optional `contextId` (absent = global scope, super-admin gated; present = that context, context-admin gated). VTA owns the `vta/*` spec namespace, so the spec change should be PR'd from here to `trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf`, with the implementation updated in `vta-service`.

## Evidence that these are one surface

- **Schemas:** each context-variant payload is byte-for-byte the global schema plus a required `contextId`, retitled descriptions, and a deeper `$ref` path. Only substantive deltas: context `render` injects ambient `CONTEXT_ID`/`CONTEXT_DID` vars, and the authorization gate differs.
- **Implementation:** both families dispatch into a single module (`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/did_templates.rs`) with paired handlers (`handle_list` / `handle_context_list`, …). Twelve URIs, one implementation.
- **History:** both families landed in the same trust-tasks PR (#89); neither supersedes the other — it's a deliberate scope split that a single optional field expresses just as well, in the style of the `provision/integration` `oneOf` precedent.
- **Smell:** `proofRequirement: REQUIRED` is blanket-stamped across the family, including pure reads (`get`, `list`, `render`), unlike the reasoned per-task levels elsewhere in the registry — consistent with mechanical duplication.

## Also in scope

- Move the ~100-line `DidTemplateRecord`/`DidTemplate` definition — currently duplicated inline in all twelve payload schemas — into `vta/_shared/` (registry-conventions issue: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#152).
- Re-derive per-task proof levels while touching the family (reads plausibly `RECOMMENDED`).

Net effect: −6 task specs, one dispatch table section, no capability loss (the per-scope ACL moves from slug-structure to the `contextId` field + party gating).

_From a cross-registry consolidation analysis, 2026-07-29._

title: feat(vtc): decide replaces approve/reject; accept folds into members/vmc; endorsement-types per-method tasks
body:
Closes #853. Spec PR (cross-linked): https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/160

Per the coordinator's policy update this is a **clean cutover**, not dual-accept: the superseded URIs are removed outright.

## Removed wire URIs — consumers to sweep

- `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/join-requests/approve/0.1` (REST `POST /v1/join-requests/{id}/approve`)
- `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/join-requests/reject/0.1` (REST `POST /v1/join-requests/{id}/reject`)
- `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/join-requests/accept/0.1` (document dispatcher + DIDComm; the `MembershipAcknowledgement` reciprocal-VC shape and the accept holder-binding signature go with it)

**Consumer note:** OpenVTC/openvtc CLI uses `join-requests/{submit,status}` and `members/self-remove` only — unaffected, but reviewers should confirm. The in-repo consumer (admin SPA `joinRequests.tsx`) is updated in this PR.

## What changed

**1. `POST /v1/join-requests/{id}/decide`** on `vtc/join-requests/decide/0.1` — `{ decision: approved|rejected, reason? }`. One handler (`decide.rs`) with the shared Pending-state gate, then the approve arm (admit + issue VMC/role-VEC, unchanged spine) or the reject arm (status flip + reason). Audit envelopes unchanged (`JoinRequestApproved`/`JoinRequestRejected`).

**2. accept → `members/vmc` + `requestId`.** `MemberVmcBody`/`MemberVmcReceiptBody` gain an optional `requestId` (string UUID — `vta_sdk::protocols::members` compiles featureless, so it avoids the optional `uuid` dep; handlers parse and refuse a malformed id). `receive_member_vmc_inner` validates the named request (exists / belongs to the proven sender / `Approved`) **before** any write, then records the stored credential as the reciprocal half (`record_reciprocation`) and audits `MembershipReciprocated`. Receipt echoes `requestId`. Deliberate behavior change vs. accept: re-delivering a *different* credential is the vmc task's renewal semantics (replaces, updates reciprocation) rather than accept's 409 — flagged for review.

**3. Per-method selectors — reality check vs. the issue.** The issue predated main's discovery that `task_routes` + axum already enforce per-method tasks on a shared path (pinned by `vti_common::trust_task::openapi`). Three of the four named remaps had **already landed on main**: members show/update/admin-remove, community profile show/update, admin join-requests list. This PR lands the last one: `GET /v1/endorsement-types` now gates on `vtc/endorsement-types/list/0.1` (published in trust-tasks-rs 0.2.43) instead of riding `register`'s URI, with a per-method gating test. Out of scope, left as-is and noted: `members/personhood` POST+DELETE still share `assert`'s URI (not in the issue's list).

**4. Census + release guards.** `vtc/join-requests/decide/0.1` is a counted exception in `UNPUBLISHED_CANONICAL_OK` until the workspace's `trust-tasks-rs` pin (0.2.43) bumps past **0.2.47** (the spec PR's release) — drop the entry on that bump. title: vtc: merge join-requests approve/reject into decide, unify accept with members/vmc, add per-method router selectors
body:
## Proposals (vtc family — owned by vtc-service, specs PR'd upstream to trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf)

### 1. Merge `vtc/join-requests/approve` + `reject` → `vtc/join-requests/decide`

Payloads are near-identical (`approve`: `{id}`; `reject`: `{id, reason?}`), same admin gate, same `pending`→`notPending` lifecycle check, same proof posture (REQUIRED/mutating), and approve's spec already calls reject "the decision counterpart". A `{id, decision: approved|rejected, reason?}` task loses nothing. This mirrors the sanctioned enum-variant pattern (`provision/integration`, `auth/passkey/login/start`'s `purpose`).

### 2. Unify `vtc/join-requests/accept` with `vtc/members/vmc`

Both carry the member-issued reciprocal credential to the community to close the bidirectional membership edge: `accept` = `{requestId, vmcId, vc}` at join time; `vmc` = `{vc}` any time, idempotent, valid unsolicited. `accept` is essentially vmc-plus-request-state-transition. Either define accept as vmc-with-optional-`requestId`, or let `vmc` close an approved join request when one is open. −1 task, one credential-delivery path instead of two.

### 3. Per-method Trust-Task selectors in `TrustTaskRouter` (unblocks real per-task enforcement)

The "Phase-0 workaround" comment appears ≥5 times in `vtc-service/src/routes/mod.rs`: because the router can't select per HTTP method, several distinct specs are enforced under a single task URI today —
- `vtc/endorsement-types/list` gated under `register`'s URI (the standalone list spec exists but is never enforced)
- `members/show` + `update` + `admin-remove` share one mount/task
- `community/profile` GET + PUT under one task
- admin `join-requests` list rides `submit`'s task

Until this lands, part of the registry's per-task granularity (and its per-task audit/gating rationale) is theoretical for vtc. Fixing the router should come first; it also tells us empirically which per-task splits vtc actually needs.

## Explicitly out of scope (analysis says keep separate)

`admin/invites` vs `invitations` (operator install URLs vs W3C member credentials — already split from a collapsed mount once, deliberately); the `solicit-vmc`/`request-vmc`/`vmc` triple ("three tasks, three party pairs"); `backup` vs `config` export/import ("this is not a backup"); `status` vs `show` (anti-probing oracle design); the challenge/finish ceremony pairs (protocol-required).

## Consumers to check

`OpenVTC/openvtc` CLI uses `join-requests/{submit,status}` and `members/self-remove` — the decide-merge is admin-side so client impact should be nil, but verify before landing.

_From a cross-registry consolidation analysis, 2026-07-29._

title: feat(did-management): state-enum consolidation — agent-name/update, did/set-state, domain/set-state; retire did/publish; spec agent-name check/list
body:
⚠️ **Version slot 0.2.50 assumed, sequenced after #162 (0.2.49) — if merge order changes or another trust-tasks PR lands first, the orchestrator must re-bump this PR before merge.**

Addresses https://github.com/affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service/issues/143

## What

Collapses the did-management state-toggle verb sets into declarative state-enum tasks, retires `did/publish` into `did/register`, and specs the two implemented-but-unspecced agent-name reads.

**New tasks (0.1, draft):**
- `did-management/agent-name/update` — `state: active | parked`, same payload fields as the retired trio (`mnemonic`, `name`, `didData` required; `domain` optional). `active` folds bind / refresh / resume into one value; `parked` keeps the reservation. Declarative: requesting the current state is an idempotent refresh (no `already_disabled` / `not_disabled` error class). **`agent-name/remove` deliberately stays its own task** — it is the family's destructive verb (a released name becomes claimable by anyone), and folding it in would force the merged task to carry the destructive side-effect class and erase the audit distinction between parking and releasing; the new spec's prose states this rationale.
- `did-management/did/set-state` — `state: active | suspended`, replacing `did/{enable,disable}` (identical payloads, mutual inverses).
- `did-management/domain/set-state` — `state: active | disabled`, replacing `domain/{enable,disable}`. `is_default` → `isDefault` and `already_purged` → `alreadyPurged` boundaries carried over as `set-state` errors.
- `did-management/agent-name/check` — read-only availability probe (free / taken / reserved), shape derived from the webvh-service implementation (`AgentNameAvailability`). No reserve mode by design.
- `did-management/agent-name/list` — owner-scoped registry listing including parked entries; `createdAt` specced as RFC3339 (impl projects from epoch seconds).

**Retired (`status: retired` + `supersededBy`, folders kept for auditability):** `agent-name/{set,enable,disable}`, `did/{enable,disable}`, `domain/{enable,disable}`, and `did/publish` → `did/register`.

**In-place draft-additive edit:** `did/register` prose now states explicitly that register fully covers the reserved-slot flow (an owner re-register is an update — the operation the retired publish carried); `agent-name/remove` prose repointed at the update task.

New specs follow the canonical lowerCamelCase error-code convention from #154; the shared `did-management:unknown_domain` family code is unchanged.

## Validation

- `npm run build` — `Validated 262 specs, indexed 46 shared schemas.` ✅
- `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all` — 261 payload modules, no drift ✅
- `npm run build-ts-bindings` — 309 TS modules; `tsc -p tsconfig.json` clean ✅
- `cargo check -p trust-tasks-rs` ✅
- Version bumps: `trust-tasks-rs` + `@openvtc/trust-tasks` set to **0.2.50** in lockstep (rebased onto 0.2.48 main; 0.2.49 is reserved for #162 which is sequenced ahead), CHANGELOG entry, `Cargo.lock` refreshed. Rebased build: `Validated 269 specs`, 267 Rust / 315 TS modules regenerated cleanly.

Version bumps / generated bindings may be rebased by the orchestrator as sibling consolidation PRs merge.

## Companion PR

Implementation (clean cutover to these URIs): https://github.com/affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service/pull/144

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] `agent-name/remove` kept separate (destructive class separately auditable) — agree with rationale?
- [ ] `domain/set-state` enum `active|disabled` (matches `DomainEntry.status`) vs the issue's `did` enum `active|suspended` — intentional per-family naming.
- [ ] Retirement markers: `status: retired` + `supersededBy` on all eight specs; prose note in each Status section.
- [ ] `agent-name/list` `createdAt` as RFC3339 (registry convention) rather than the implementation's raw epoch — impl PR projects accordingly.

body:
Addresses https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/issues/853 (spec side; implementation PR: https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/863).

## What changed

**New task: `vtc/join-requests/decide/0.1`** — one admin decision payload, `{ id, decision: approved|rejected, reason? }`, REQUIRED proof, `mutating`, with the error vocabulary covering the shared lifecycle check: `decide:permissionDenied`, `decide:notFound`, `decide:notPending`. The approve/reject pair had near-identical payloads, the same admin gate, the same pending-state check and the same proof posture; the decision is one enum field, not two tasks (the sanctioned enum-variant pattern — `provision/integration`, `auth/passkey/login/start`'s `purpose`).

**`vtc/members/vmc/0.1` gains an optional `requestId`** (in-place additive edit — the spec is `draft`). When present and naming an approved join request whose applicant is the delivering member, the delivery also closes that request, recording the delivered credential as the reciprocal half of the join; the receipt echoes `requestId`. New error codes: `requestNotFound`, `requestNotApproved`, `requestApplicantMismatch`. The accept-vs-vmc rationale is written into the spec prose: both tasks carried the same member-issued credential to the same recipient to close the membership edge — accept was vmc plus a request-state transition, so the registry keeps one credential-delivery path.

**Retired** (folders kept, `status: retired` + `supersededBy` per SPEC §5.3 / §7.3 item 11, tombstone note in the prose):
- `vtc/join-requests/approve/0.1` → `vtc/join-requests/decide`
- `vtc/join-requests/reject/0.1` → `vtc/join-requests/decide`
- `vtc/join-requests/accept/0.1` → `vtc/members/vmc`

**Housekeeping** per the release rules: Rust + TS bindings regenerated; `trust-tasks-rs` and `@openvtc/trust-tasks` bumped 0.2.46 → **0.2.47** (lockstep), CHANGELOG entry added, `Cargo.lock` refreshed.

- [ ] Retirement markers: `status: retired` + `supersededBy` on approve/reject/accept, prose tombstones read correctly

Addresses https://github.com/affinidi/affinidi-trust-registry-rs/issues/120 (spec side).
Implementation PR (clean cutover in the trust registry): https://github.com/affinidi/affinidi-trust-registry-rs/pull/121

## What

**New tasks**

- **`registry/record/put/0.1`** — create-or-replace on the single `record: TrustRecord` payload. Following the `vault/upsert` precedent, the strict semantics of the superseded pair survive as an optional assertion: `expectedExisting: false` = strict create (`put:alreadyExists` on conflict), `expectedExisting: true` = strict update (`put:notFound` on miss), absent = pure upsert. Response carries `ok` + `created`.
- **`registry/record/query/0.1`** — optional four-part TRQP key. All four supplied: exact fetch, `query:notFound` on a miss (preserving read's absent-vs-empty distinction for admin tooling). Fewer supplied: filtered enumeration with `cursor`/`limit` (1..=200, default 50) pagination and `nextCursor` — fixing the pagination gap `record/list`'s own abstract conceded.
- **`registry/did/rotate/0.1`** — new spec documenting a **pre-existing live wire contract** in affinidi-trust-registry-rs (VTA-backed `did:webvh` key rotation; README-documented, admin-ACL + proof gated). Field names are frozen snake_case from the deployed wire form. Authored rather than removed per issue item 4, because the reference is a real handler, not vestigial.

**Retired** (folders kept, schemas frozen, `supersededBy` set):

- `registry/record/create/0.1`, `registry/record/update/0.1` → `registry/record/put`
- `registry/record/read/0.1`, `registry/record/list/0.1` → `registry/record/query`

**Deliberately untouched:** `registry/authorization` / `registry/recognition` — the two-task split mirrors TRQP v2.0's two endpoints (issue item 3: no change).

Conventions: new tasks target framework 0.2 with camelCase for new fields/error codes; the four TRQP key fields and the `TrustRecord` shape stay verbatim-TRQP snake_case, as documented throughout the `registry/*` family. `related` links in `record/delete`, `recognition`, `authorization` repointed at the successors.

## Housekeeping

- Regenerated Rust bindings (`trust-tasks-codegen` + `cargo fmt`) and TS bindings.
- `trust-tasks-rs` + `@openvtc/trust-tasks` bumped **0.2.45 → 0.2.46** in lockstep; CHANGELOG entry; `Cargo.lock` refreshed.
- Rebased onto main after #153–#157.

Version bumps / generated bindings may be rebased by the orchestrator as sibling consolidation PRs merge.

## Validation

- `npm run build` — `Validated 260 specs, indexed 46 shared schemas.` Done, no warnings.
- `cargo check -p trust-tasks-rs` — clean; `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs` — pass.
- Codegen re-run post-rebase produced no drift beyond the intended new modules.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] `expectedExisting` tri-state semantics on put match the vault/upsert precedent you'd expect.
- [ ] query's fully-keyed-miss-is-an-error (vs empty page on partial key) is the right call for admin tooling (registry-wide house style per #152).
- [ ] `registry/did/rotate` frontmatter: `sideEffects: destructive` and snake_case wire-freeze rationale.
- [ ] Retirement edits limited to `status`/`supersededBy` + the Status-of-this-Document paragraph.

title: feat(push): cut push/* emitters over to 0.2 wire (gateway cutover sweep)
body:
Addresses OpenVTC/vti-push-gateway#21 consumer sweep.

**Merge-order note: this must merge (and deploy) before the gateway 0.2 cutover (OpenVTC/vti-push-gateway#21) deploys against these services** — the gateway now rejects push/* 0.1 documents.

## What changed

Clean cutover of all VTI push/* emitters to the 0.2 URIs — no dual-emit. Request payloads are field-identical 0.1→0.2; the only wire-visible change is the push/wake response status enum `token-unregistered` → `tokenUnregistered`.

- **vta-service `trust_tasks/device.rs`** — set-wake gateway provisioning now emits `push/provision/0.2`.
- **vta-service `trust_tasks/step_up.rs`** — the step-up wake trigger now emits `push/wake/0.2`, and now **parses the gateway's response status** (previously discarded) via the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs::push::wake::v0_2::ResponseStatus`: `tokenUnregistered` (dead platform token; handle dropped) logs a warning — mediator-queue fallback applies; `delivered` logs info. The retired kebab-case `token-unregistered` is deliberately NOT accepted (clean cutover).
- **vta-sdk `agent_session.rs`** — inbound-wake test fixture moved to the 0.2 URI.
- **vta-mobile-core `push.rs`** — verified already on `push/register/0.2`; it parses no wake status anywhere. Unchanged.
- Release guards: vta-service 0.13.8 → **0.13.9**, vta-sdk 0.20.16 → **0.20.17**, root `CHANGELOG.md` entry under Unreleased, `Cargo.lock` refreshed.

## Discrepancies vs. the gateway PR's consumer list

- `vta-sdk/src/agent_session.rs` does **not** emit push/wake — it only *parses* an inbound wake envelope (type string is opaque to the parser; only a test fixture cited the 0.1 URI), and it never inspects the wake response status. Fixture updated; no behavior change.
- No code in VTI parsed the wake response status at all before this PR; the `tokenUnregistered` handling in `step_up.rs` is new (and is where the renamed enum value becomes wire-visible to VTI).

## Version-bump caveat

vta-service 0.13.9 assumes #858 (which also bumps vta-service) has not merged yet — if it lands first, this PR takes 0.13.10 and a small CHANGELOG rebase (orchestrator-coordinated).

## Test evidence

```
cargo check -p vta-service -p vta-sdk                       → Finished dev profile
cargo test -p vta-service --lib step_up                     → 21 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p vta-service --lib wake_reply_status           → 3 passed; 0 failed (new)
cargo test -p vta-sdk --features session --lib agent_session → 5 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p vta-mobile-core --lib push                    → 7 passed; 0 failed
cargo fmt -p vta-service -p vta-sdk --check                 → clean
```

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Confirm clean cutover is intended (no dual-emit window on the VTA side) and that this merges/deploys before the gateway cutover.
- [ ] `wake_reply_status` returning `None` for the legacy kebab-case value only affects a log line (best-effort path) — confirm that's acceptable vs. hard-failing.
- [ ] Version bumps: vta-service 0.13.9 / vta-sdk 0.20.17 vs. #858 ordering.

title: feat(vta-sdk): sign() reaches TSP via the Trust-Task bridge — and every twinned rpc method moves with it (#829)
body:
Closes https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/issues/829

## What

`VtaClient::sign()` was the only signing entry point that could not reach TSP — it rode the legacy `rpc` path whose TSP arm is `Err(unsupported_over_tsp(..))`. It now routes through `rpc_tt(TASK_KEYS_SIGN_1_0, …)`, keeping `POST /keys/{key_id}/sign` as the REST leg — exactly the shape `derive_and_sign` beside it already has.

The issue's last paragraph asked which other `rpc`/`rpc_void`-routed methods with an existing Trust Task twin should move at the same time. This PR audits **all 42** remaining `rpc`/`rpc_void` call sites against the current dispatcher (`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs`) and moves **every method whose request AND response wire shapes already match its twin** — the sweeping form the issue gestures at, on pre-production code. Nothing server-side changes: legacy DIDComm message handlers remain, so existing clients keep working (nothing to dual-accept — the dispatcher already served all of these URIs).

Note (re. the issue text vs. current main): the issue named the keys/seeds/ACL slices as having twins. Latest main has grown twins for contexts, audit, config, management, discovery, and webvh as well; the audit below covers all of them.

## Audit table: method → task URI → moved?

| Client method | Trust Task URI | Moved? |
|---|---|---|
| `sign` | `vta/keys/sign/1.0` | **moved** (the headline fix) |
| `list_keys` / `create_key` / `get_key` / `rename_key` / `invalidate_key` | `vta/keys/{list,create,get,rename,revoke}/1.0` | moved |
| `get_key_secret` | `vta/seeds/export-mnemonic/1.0` | moved — same `{key_id}` body, same `operations::keys::get_key_secret` spine |
| `list_seeds` / `rotate_seed` | `vta/seeds/{list,rotate}/1.0` | moved |
| `create_acl` | `acl/grant/0.1` | moved — `CreateAclRequest` already serializes the canonical `{entry}` body |
| `delete_acl` | `acl/revoke/0.1` | moved (`rpc_tt_void`) |
| `list_audit_logs` | `audit/list/0.1` | moved — request conformance is asserted in `trust_tasks::audit::tests` |
| `get_audit_retention` / `update_audit_retention` | `vta/audit/{get,update}-retention/1.0` | moved |
| `list_contexts` / `get_context` / `create_context` / `update_context` / `update_context_did` / `preview_delete_context` / `delete_context` | `vta/contexts/*/1.0` | moved |
| `get_config` / `update_config` | `config/show/0.1` / `config/patch/0.1` | moved — `UpdateConfigRequest` flattens to the canonical `{overrides}` |
| `restart` | `vta/management/reload-services/1.0` | moved (registry doc's mapping for `POST /vta/restart`) |
| `capabilities` | `vta/discovery/capabilities/1.0` | moved |
| `add_webvh_server` / `list_webvh_servers` / `remove_webvh_server` | `vta/webvh/servers/{register,list,remove}/1.0` | moved |
| `create_did_webvh` / `list_dids_webvh` / `get_did_webvh` / `delete_did_webvh` / `register_did_with_server` | `vta/webvh/dids/*/1.0` | moved |
| `get_did_webvh_log` | `vta/webvh/dids/get/1.0` + `includeLog: true` | moved — the get-log task folded into `dids/get`; the flattened response is a strict superset of `GetDidLogResponse` |
| `list_acl` / `list_acl_in_direction` | `acl/list/0.1` | **not moved** — the twin's response is a bare array of the flat stored form, not the canonical `{entries, truncated, …}` the client (and REST leg) decode; request also renames `context`→`scope`. → #857 |
| `get_acl` | `acl/show/0.1` | **not moved** — twin returns flat `CreateAclResultBody`, not the canonical `{entry}` envelope the client decodes (`handle_get` calls `operations::acl::get_acl` instead of `show_by_subject`). → #857 |
| `change_acl_role` | `acl/change-role/0.1` | **not moved** — same flat-response drift (`handle_change_role` → `change_role`, not a wrapped op). → #857 |
| `update_acl` | `acl/update/0.1` | **not moved** — request shape is non-canonical (`did`/`allowed_contexts` vs required `subject`/`scopes`) and the dispatch spine schema-rejects it today; documented in `trust_tasks/acl.rs` tests. → #857 |
| `swap_acl` | `acl/swap-key/0.1` | **not moved** — canonical body needs `currentSubject`/`newSubject`; the client API carries only the VP-JWT. Needs a (breaking) client-API change first. → #857 |
| `update_webvh_server` | (`vta/webvh/servers/register/1.0` absorbs update) | **not moved** — twin is register-or-update: a typo'd id would silently create a server instead of 404ing. Behavioural change, flagged rather than papered over. → #857 |
| `update_did_webvh` / `rotate_did_webvh_keys` | `vta/webvh/dids/{update,rotate-keys}/1.0` | **not moved** — twins address the DID by `did` (flattened body); the client addresses by `context_id`+`scid`. `dids/update` is additionally schema-validated. → #857 |
| `import_key` | — | no twin (`keys/import` not dispatched) → drift input for #854 |
| `get_wrapping_key` | — | no twin; REST-only by design (wrapping key exists only for REST import) → #854 triage can confirm |
| `list_webvh_server_domains` | — | no twin → #854 |
| `backup_export` / `backup_import` | — | no *direct* twin — the trust-task backup slice is the five-step descriptor protocol (`initiate/complete-export`, `initiate/finalize-import`, `abort`), a different wire contract → #854/#857 |

## Observable wire-behaviour notes (beyond the transport envelope)

- DIDComm/TSP legs of moved methods now pass through the trust-task dispatch spine: PDP policy gate, replay guard, and payload-schema validation for the published URIs (`acl/grant`, `acl/revoke`, `audit/list`, `config/show`, `config/patch`). All moved payloads were verified against those schemas (no nulls where the schema types a string; `additionalProperties: false` respected). The `vta/*` URIs in this sweep have no published schema and dispatch unvalidated.
- `create_key` over trust task auto-generates the key id (`handle_create` pins `key_id: None`) — identical to the legacy DIDComm message, which never carried `key_id`; explicit ids remain a REST-leg feature.
- Errors on the DIDComm leg now surface as trust-task rejections (`VtaError::Protocol`/task-rejection mapping) rather than legacy problem-reports — same as the already-migrated `derive_and_sign`/`did_templates` surfaces.
- `rpc_void` lost its last caller and is removed from the SDK (internal, `pub(super)`).

## Validation

- `cargo check -p vta-sdk -p vta-service --all-features` — clean (no warnings).
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --all-features --lib` — **540 passed, 0 failed**.
- `cargo test -p vta-service --all-features --lib` — **729 passed, 0 failed** (includes the trust-task dispatch/schema-gate suites).
- Release guards: `vta-sdk` bumped 0.20.16 → 0.20.17 with a root `CHANGELOG.md` entry under Unreleased. (`vta-service` untouched. Expect a trivial CHANGELOG rebase if #858 merges first.)

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Each moved method's TT handler parses the same protocol body the client sends (spot-check `keys::handle_sign`, `seeds::handle_export_mnemonic`, `webvh::handle_dids_get`).
- [ ] Agree the not-moved rows are #857/#854 material rather than blockers here.
- [ ] `get_did_webvh_log` via `dids/get` + `includeLog`: flattened superset decodes as `GetDidLogResponse` (fields `did`, `log`).
- [ ] Removal of `rpc_void` is acceptable (internal helper, zero callers).

title: VtaClient::sign() is the only signing entry point that cannot reach TSP
body:
`keys.rs` has three signing entry points. Two of them route through the Trust-Task bridge and therefore work on every transport; the primary one does not.

| Method | Routes via | Works on TSP |
|---|---|---|
| `derive_and_sign` | `rpc_tt(TASK_KEYS_DERIVE_AND_SIGN_1_0, …)` (`vta-sdk/src/client/keys.rs:149`) | yes |
| `derive_and_sign_document` | `rpc_tt(TASK_KEYS_DERIVE_AND_SIGN_DOCUMENT_1_0, …)` (`keys.rs:176`) | yes |
| **`sign`** | `rpc(key_management::SIGN_REQUEST, …)` (`keys.rs:105`) | **no** |

`rpc` and `rpc_void` both end in `Transport::Tsp { .. } => Err(unsupported_over_tsp(msg_type))` (`client/mod.rs:1140`, `1172`), so a TSP client calling the raw-bytes signing oracle gets `UnsupportedTransport` — while the same client can derive-and-sign perfectly well.

## Everything needed for the fix already exists

- The Trust Task is defined and handled: `spec/vta/keys/sign/1.0` / `TASK_KEYS_SIGN_1_0` (`trust_tasks.rs:301`), handler `handle_sign` (`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/keys.rs:168`), reaching the identical `operations::keys::sign_payload` spine with the same `{ key_id, payload, algorithm }` body and the same base64url conventions.
- The bridge exists and is the documented pattern for exactly this: `rpc_tt` keeps the dedicated REST route while the DIDComm leg dispatches the Trust Task, and its TSP arm notes the surface "needed no per-operation work to reach TSP".

So the change looks like moving `sign()` from `rpc` to `rpc_tt` with `TASK_KEYS_SIGN_1_0`, keeping `POST /keys/{key_id}/sign` as the REST leg — the same shape `derive_and_sign` beside it already has. The three signing paths then behave identically across transports instead of one being the odd one out.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

A consumer that signs through the VTA and is migrating DIDComm → TSP finds that its *one* VTA call is the one that doesn't port. Cierge's gateway is that consumer: signing is the only VTA operation it performs, so `sign()` alone decides whether its sessions are transport-agnostic. It can work around this today by calling `dispatch_trust_task(TASK_KEYS_SIGN_1_0, …)` directly and hand-decoding the payload — but a workaround that re-implements a typed method in every consumer is the argument for fixing it here, not there.

Worth deciding alongside: whether any other `rpc`-routed methods with an existing Trust Task twin should move at the same time (the keys, seeds and ACL slices in `docs/05-design-notes/trust-task-uri-registry.md` all list one), or whether `sign` is pulled forward on its own because it is the operation consumers actually build on.

Related: affinidi/cierge#48, and `docs/design-context-hierarchy.md` in that repo, where the per-domain signing session is specified against the Trust Task for this reason.
author: stormer78

title: feat(vta-sdk): route every trust-task-twinned client method through rpc_tt (#829) (#861)
body:
feat(vta-sdk): route every trust-task-twinned client method through rpc_tt (#829) (#861)

VtaClient::sign() was the only signing entry point that could not reach
TSP: it rode the legacy rpc path, whose TSP arm returns
UnsupportedTransport. It now dispatches spec/vta/keys/sign/1.0 through
rpc_tt, keeping POST /keys/{key_id}/sign as the REST leg — the same
shape derive_and_sign beside it already has.

The issue's closing question — which other rpc-routed methods with an
existing Trust Task twin should move — was audited against the
dispatcher and acted on. Everything whose request AND response wire
shapes already match its twin moves in this sweep:

- keys: list/create/get/rename/revoke/sign; get_key_secret via
  vta/seeds/export-mnemonic (same {key_id} body, same
  operations::keys::get_key_secret spine)
- seeds: list, rotate
- acl: create (client already serializes canonical acl/grant {entry}),
  delete (acl/revoke {subject})
- audit: list (canonical audit/list/0.1, conformance-tested),
  retention get/update
- contexts: list/get/create/update/update-did/preview-delete/delete
- config: show/patch; restart via vta/management/reload-services;
  capabilities via vta/discovery/capabilities
- webvh: servers register/list/remove, dids
  create/list/get/get-log/delete/register-with-server (dids/get
  returns the record flattened, a strict superset of both legacy
  response shapes)

NOT moved, with reasons recorded for the conformance stream (#857) and
registry-drift triage (#854): list_acl/get_acl/change_acl_role (twin
responses are the flat stored form, not the canonical {entry}/{entries}
envelopes), update_acl (request non-canonical; schema-rejected by the
dispatch spine), swap_acl (canonical body needs subjects the client API
does not carry), update_webvh_server (twin is register-or-update),
update_did_webvh/rotate_did_webvh_keys (twin addresses by did, client
by context_id+scid), and the twinless import_key, get_wrapping_key,
list_webvh_server_domains, backup_export/backup_import.

rpc_void lost its last caller and is removed. REST behaviour is
unchanged on every method; server-side legacy DIDComm handlers remain,
so old clients keep working.

Closes #829

title: feat(parity): reverse registry-parity harness, per-URI drift triage, and the vta-sdk constant rename pass (#854 phase 1)
body:
Closes https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/issues/854 (phase 1 — triage + guard; the registry PRs implementing the dispositions are follow-on tranches).

## What changed

**1. Reverse parity harness** (`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs`). The existing harness asserts every `vta-sdk` URI is served; nothing asserted the opposite. `every_served_uri_has_a_published_spec_or_is_tracked_debt` now requires every URI the VTA serves — dispatched, REST-routed, feature-gated, or `wire_v0_2` edge-transformed — to resolve in the published registry via the generated `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index` (the registry index vendored through the pinned crate; the in-repo `trust-tasks/index.json` is the retired `openvtc/vtc` authority and was not usable for this). The 56 known-unspecced URIs sit in `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS`, per-URI, annotated with the tracking issue. The harness fails on: any NEW unspecced served URI, any allowlist entry whose spec has since been published upstream (the list only shrinks), and any entry no longer served. Complements — does not replace — the workspace census in `vtc-service/tests/trust_task_manifest.rs` (#821), which is source-literal + per-family-count based.

**2. Triage doc** — `docs/05-design-notes/registry-drift-triage.md`. Tabulates all 56 implemented-but-unspecced URIs with a keep-and-spec / fold / delete disposition each (aggressive, per the pre-production policy), the version-straddle list (`auth/step-up/approve-request` 0.2, `device/wipe/0.2` missing from `wire_v0_2`, `policy/evaluate`/`policy/delete` unreferenced), and corrections to the issue's enumeration re-derived from latest main:
- `consent/approve-request/0.1` does not exist (the real family is `task-consent/*`; `request/0.1` is published);
- `vtc/auth/login/0.1` and monolithic `vtc/install/claim/0.1|0.2` are bound by **no route** — they survive only as `vti-common` test-fixture/doc-example strings; the start/finish claim shape already won;
- `task-consent/granted/0.1` excluded as in-flight (sibling stream).
Slotted into the `canonical-task-reduction.md` programme (§A–§F references); sibling streams #856 (acl/update body) and #857 (payload-conformance sweep) are referenced, not duplicated.

**3. The `_1_0` rename pass** (`vta-sdk/src/trust_tasks.rs` + 2 consumer files). Ten constants whose greppable name lied about the wire (`TASK_ACL_LIST_1_0` naming `acl/list/0.1`) renamed to canonical verb stem + true version suffix: `TASK_ACL_{LIST,GRANT,SHOW,UPDATE,REVOKE,SWAP_KEY}_0_1`, `TASK_AUDIT_LIST_0_1`, `TASK_CONFIG_{SHOW,PATCH}_0_1`, `TASK_PROVISION_INTEGRATION_0_2`. A new source-scanning guard (`constant_suffix_matches_uri_version`) pins suffix = URI version for every literal-assigned constant. **Constant renames only — no wire URI changed.** Regenerating `trust-task-uri-registry.md` from the constants is scoped to tranche 2 in the triage doc (it is a doc rewrite, not a mechanical pass).

Release housekeeping: vta-sdk 0.20.16 → 0.20.17, vta-service 0.13.8 → 0.13.9, root `CHANGELOG.md` entry, `Cargo.lock` refreshed. Version bumps may be rebased by the orchestrator as sibling consolidation PRs merge.

## Evidence

```
cargo test -p vta-sdk --lib      → 220 passed; 0 failed
```

title: Reconcile registry↔implementation drift for VTA-owned task families (~45 unspecced URIs, version straddles)
body:
## Problem

The registry (`trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf`) and this implementation have drifted in **both directions**. Since the consumer/server side owns its spec families, closing the gap is work that lives here.

### Implemented URIs with no spec folder in the registry (~45)

- The whole `vta/*` 1.0 surface: `vta/keys/*`, `vta/contexts/*` (beyond did-templates), `vta/seeds/*`, `vta/audit/*`, `vta/backup/*`, `vta/attestation/*`, `vta/discovery/capabilities`, `vta/management/reload-services`, `vta/webvh/**` beyond `dids/update`
- `vault/{archive,unarchive,restore,purge}/0.1` and all eight `vault/credentials/*/0.1`
- `task-consent/granted/0.1` (see the confirm-retirement issue), `consent/approve-request/0.1`
- `vtc/auth/login/0.1`; `vtc/install/claim/0.1|0.2` (registry has `claim/{start,finish}/0.1` instead — both shapes referenced somewhere)

Each of these is a live wire contract with no published schema, no registry page, no generated bindings, and no discovery entry.

### Registry versions this repo has skipped or straddled

- `auth/step-up/approve-request/0.2` unimplemented (0.1 in use) while `approve-response` dual-accepts 0.1|0.2 in a single match arm
- `device/wipe/0.2` is the only device 0.2 missing from the `wire_v0_2` table
- `policy/evaluate` (all three versions) and `policy/delete/0.1` unreferenced
- Constant-name drift acknowledged in `vta-sdk/src/trust_tasks.rs` ("`_1_0` suffix … rename pass" pending), with every const mirrored by hand in `docs/05-design-notes/trust-task-uri-registry.md`

### Root-cause item

`wire_v0_2.rs` exists solely because ten 0.1→0.2 registry bumps changed enum casing only. A registry-side versioning-policy fix is proposed as trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#151 — once adopted, the adapter can stop growing.

## Suggested approach

1. Triage the ~45 unspecced URIs: spec the keepers (PR to the registry), delete/alias the accidental ones.
2. Decide `vtc/install/claim` shape (monolithic vs start/finish) and make code + registry agree.
3. Do the vta-sdk constant rename pass and generate the URI doc from the constants instead of hand-mirroring.
4. Add a CI parity check in the opposite direction of the existing one: every dispatched URI must have a registry spec (the current harness only checks every SDK constant is dispatched).

_From a cross-registry consolidation analysis, 2026-07-29._

title: docs(design): governance policy as a credential — closing #804 with zero new tasks
body:
**Design for review — implementation deliberately deferred pending sign-off.**

Addresses https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/issues/804 (V2, adopted by the Cierge side 2026-07-26).

Companion registry PR (draft spec changes implementing the recommendation): https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/157

## What this adds

`docs/05-design-notes/governance-policy-credential.md` — a design note in the house style of `multi-tenant-signing.md` / `canonical-task-reduction.md`, laying out how the VTA issues a domain's governance policy (model allowlist, budget, upstream pin, privacy tier) as a Verifiable Credential so attestations cite a `policyHash` whose issuance chain a verifier can check.

The overriding constraint was **everything on defined trust tasks with defined specs, as minimal as possible**. The recommendation carries all three of #804's asks on existing tasks — **zero new trust tasks**:

| #804 ask | Carried by |
|---|---|
| Issuance | `vta/credentials/issue/0.1` + a `GovernancePolicyCredential` claims profile (step-up-gated rotation; single-active supersession returning `supersedes`, mirroring `policy/activate`'s `previousPolicyId`) |
| Revocation | `vta/credentials/revoke/0.1` + mandatory published `credentialStatus` (adopts the `vtc/endorsements` status-list mechanics — bit flip, slot never reclaimed — without adopting that family's plane) |
| Distribution | `credential-exchange/query` → `present`, VTA as holder of the profile credentials it mints |

Options evaluated and rejected with reasons: piggybacking the VC on `policy/activate` (wrong artifact — registry `PolicyModule` is Rego decision source, not enforcement parameters; wrong surface — the VTA binds no `policy/*` task, only `vtc-service` does; not additive to a shipped contract) and reusing the `vtc/endorsements` family itself (wrong plane; its revocation mechanics are adopted instead).

The note includes the trust argument for why the chain host→VTA closes #804's gap (and what it deliberately does not fix — the #817 witness residual), precise revocation semantics (supersession vs emergency revoke, fail-closed consumption), and an implementation sketch naming touched crates (`vta-service` operations/status-list producer, `vta-keyspaces`, `vta-sdk` wire types — additive only, no URI changes so no `wire_v0_2.rs` dual-accept work). #817 / #805 scope boundaries are stated up front, as the issue draws them.

## Validation

Docs-only: no code, no version bumps (release-guards CI excludes docs-only changes). Design-note facts re-verified against current `origin/main` (post \#855): `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/credentials.rs`, `vta-service/src/operations/credentials.rs`, `vtc-service/src/routes/mod.rs:770-800`, `vta-vault/src/status.rs:21`, `vta-sdk/src/client/keys.rs:97`.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Do the #817/#805 scope boundaries read correctly (this note claims to fix rule-fabrication, not witness compromise)?
- [ ] Is the claims-profile route on `vta/credentials/issue` preferable to a new task family for you as VTA implementers?
- [ ] Comfortable with the VTA growing a status-list **producer** (currently only `vtc-service` publishes; `vta-vault/src/status.rs:21` already flags the keyspace as follow-up)?
- [ ] Distribution semantics: VTA as `credential-exchange` holder of credentials it issued — acceptable, or does that push toward a future `vta/credentials/list` read pair?

title: V2: issue governance policy as a credential
body:
Raised from a trust-model review of Cierge's LLM gateway attestation. **Adopted by the Cierge side on 2026-07-26** (V2 accepted; a companion proposal, V1, was declined). Written to stand alone — the originating design note lives outside version control.

## The problem it solves

Cierge's gateway attaches a governance attestation to LLM traffic. A verifier is meant to conclude: *"this request was subject to policy P, and P is the policy authorized for domain D."*

It cannot. The policy the gateway enforces — model allowlist, budget cap, upstream pin, privacy tier — arrives from a TOML file **on the gateway host**. Nothing binds an attestation to a policy any party other than that host agreed to, so the claim has no referent. Compromise the host and it attests happily under attacker-chosen rules.

Two fixes that look like they'd work, and don't:

- **A TEE** protects the key and can remote-attest the *code*, but not the *inputs*. The enclave faithfully signs attestations under attacker-chosen policy — the signature is honest, the rules are a lie.
- **Moving the key to the VTA** (`VtaClient::sign`) makes it non-exportable, audited and revocable — all genuinely valuable — but `sign(key_id, payload)` is a **blind oracle**. It endorses whatever bytes it is handed and has no idea what it just said.

## What's asked for

The VTA issues a domain's governance policy as a verifiable credential:

1. **Issuance** — a policy VC over the governing parameters (allowlist, budget, upstream, tier), bound to the domain/context.
2. **Revocation** — so a superseded policy stops being citable.
3. **Distribution** — a way for the enforcing component to fetch the current credential for a domain it serves.

Then an attestation cites `policyHash`, and a verifier checks the chain: *this hash is a policy the VTA issued for this domain and has not revoked.* The trust root for policy moves off the enforcing host, which is where every other authority in this stack already lives.

## The argument that may matter more than attestation

This retires host-editable policy config. On the Cierge side it structurally closes two open gaps that are currently mitigated only by an operator configuring things correctly — a model allowlist that is fail-closed by validation rather than provenance, and a privacy-tier cross-check that only happens if someone points the gateway at the right file.

## Honest scope

- This does **not** make attestation proof of compliance. Whatever sits in the request path is the witness, and a compromised witness can lie about what passed through it. That part is irreducible. What V2 removes is the ability to fabricate *what the rules were*.
- Consuming it properly means the enforcing component loads policy **out of** the credential, not merely cites it. Citation alone is tamper-evident at best — and with V1 declined there is no issuance-side check that the cited policy matches the enforced one.

Cierge-side tracking: affinidi/cierge#44 (blocked on this), affinidi/cierge#46 (consume it correctly).

title: fix(task-consent): frame the granted notice as a Trust Task document (confirm/* retirement, VTI side)
body:
Closes #852 Implementation side of the confirm→task-consent consolidation (stream `s2-confirm-retire`). Spec PR: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#156 (specs `task-consent/granted/0.1`, adds the untrusted `note` to `task-consent/request/0.1`, retires `confirm/{request,response}/0.1`). ## What changed **One fix: the `task-consent/granted/0.1` push now sends a Trust Task document.** `push_granted` sent a bare `{status, payloadDigest, taskType}` object as the DIDComm body. The DIDComm binding deserialises the body as a Trust Task document (`TrustTask

`), and the sibling `task-consent/request` push already sends complete documents — so a conforming consumer could never have parsed the granted notice. The payload is unchanged (the spec was authored from this exact shape); it just gained the required envelope (`id`, `type`, `threadId` = wire digest, `issuer`/`recipient`, `issuedAt`). Unsigned, per the spec's OPTIONAL proof: the notice is non-load-bearing (the single-use grant lookup at re-submit is the real gate) and the authcrypt sender is the attribution. ## What was verified, not changed - **There is no confirm handler to remove.** Verified: no `confirm/request/0.1` or `confirm/response/0.1` URI appears anywhere in VTI source (dispatch table in `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs`, SDK constants in `vta-sdk/src/trust_tasks.rs`). The only "confirm" hit is an unrelated comment about did-management's legacy confirm/offer DIDComm message pairs. Retiring the confirm specs removes nothing here, and per the clean-cutover policy there are no old URIs to dual-accept. - **The granted wire shape matches the new spec** — the spec was derived from this code, and the decision handler (`task_consent.rs`) needed no change. - **No `note` threading is possible.** The new `task-consent/request.note` field is requester-authored, but VTI's consent requests are minted by the policy gate from a rejected task submission, and task payload schemas are closed — there is no channel through which a requester supplies display text today. Nothing to thread; wiring one up (e.g. via a submission envelope member) would be a new feature, not part of this consolidation. ## Validation - `cargo check -p vta-service` ✔ (didcomm is a default feature, so the changed path compiles) - `cargo test -p vta-service --lib consent` — 19 passed, 0 failed ✔ ## Coordination notes - affinidi-webvh-service's dangling `confirm/request/0.1` reference is handled by the did-management stream (affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#143). - OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin showed no trust-task URI references in source, but reviewers should confirm its approval UI doesn't render confirm prompts by other means. ## Reviewer checklist - [ ] The granted envelope fields match `task-consent/granted/0.1` (spec PR above); payload untouched. - [ ] Comfortable shipping the envelope fix without a transition shim — no in-repo consumer parses the old bare body, and the notice is explicitly non-load-bearing (worst case: one poll cycle). - [ ] Agree no confirm handling exists to remove and no note-threading path exists today.

title: Retire confirm/* in favour of task-consent/* (and spec the missing task-consent/granted)
body:
## Proposal

Retire the `confirm/{request,response}/0.1` spec family in favour of `task-consent/{request,decision}` (marking `confirm/*` `supersededBy` in the registry), and spec the missing `task-consent/granted/0.1`. VTI owns/implements task-consent, so the supersession should be driven from here.

## Evidence

- **Structural subsumption:** a confirm is a task-consent with empty `effects`, `minApprovals: 1`, and a requester-authored `reason`. Everything confirm can express, task-consent can.
- **task-consent's own spec is a rebuttal of confirm's trust model:** it argues the requester-authored payload is "authored by the least trusted party in the system" and requires `effects` to be produced by dry-running the real handler. confirm's spec requires the wallet to display `payload.reason` verbatim — exactly the model task-consent rejects.
- **No mutual citation:** neither family references the other anywhere — parallel invention, not deliberate layering.
- **Implementation reality:** VTI implements task-consent end-to-end (`task_consent.rs`; `policy_gate.rs:182` mints `task-consent/request`) and has **no confirm handler**. The code also references `task-consent/granted/0.1`, which has **no spec folder** in the registry — that gap gets fixed as part of this.
- Related: `confirm/*` is also near-isomorphic to `auth/step-up/approve-{request,response}` (same `subject/challenge/reason/decision` core), so retiring confirm removes the middle member of a three-way overlap.

## Coordination needed

- `affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service` contains a reference to `confirm/request/0.1` — needs migrating to task-consent (or dropping if dead).
- `OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin` approval UI may render confirm prompts — verify and migrate if so.
- If a human-readable requester note is genuinely needed, add an explicitly-untrusted `note` field to `task-consent/request` rather than keeping a second family for it.

Net effect: −2 task specs (+1 new spec for the already-implemented `granted`), one fewer approval pattern for wallets to implement.

_From a cross-registry consolidation analysis, 2026-07-29._

title: feat(vta/credentials): GovernancePolicyCredential claims profile — governance policy as a credential (design)
body:
**Design for review — implementation deliberately deferred pending sign-off.**

Addresses https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/issues/804 (V2, adopted by the Cierge side 2026-07-26).

Companion VTI design-note PR: https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/859

## What changed and why

#804 asks for the VTA to issue a domain's governance policy as a Verifiable Credential (issuance, revocation, distribution), so an attestation can cite a `policyHash` whose chain a verifier can check. The overriding constraint was **everything on defined trust tasks, as minimal as possible** — so this PR adds **zero new tasks**. All changes are draft-additive, in-place edits to two existing `draft` specs:

### `vta/credentials/issue/0.1`
- New **claims profile** concept: a `credentialType` value may bind `claims` to a shape + extra rules; untyped shares stay fully opaque.
- **`GovernancePolicyCredential`** profile: `GovernancePolicyClaims` $def (`domain`, `policy` — the complete governing parameter document the enforcer MUST load from, `policyHash` — multihash over JCS(policy), optional `contextId`/`policyMediaType`); consumer recomputes `policyHash` and refuses mismatch with new error code `profileViolation`.
- **Single-active rule**: issuing a successor atomically revokes the predecessor, returned as new optional response field `supersedes` (mirrors `policy/activate`'s `previousPolicyId` auditability). Rotation is one task invocation.
- **Published revocation**: profile credentials MUST carry `credentialStatus` resolvable without authenticating to the VTA (adopts `vtc/endorsements` status-list mechanics without adopting that family's plane).
- **Distribution reuses `credential-exchange/query` → `present`** (VTA as holder of the credentials it mints under this profile; DCQL type discriminator + domain constraint). No new fetch task.
- Worked example; `knownImplementations` added per the new #153 convention.

### `vta/credentials/revoke/0.1`
- Published-status semantics (bit flip; slot never reclaimed) and new optional response field `statusListIndex`, mirroring `vtc/endorsements/revoke`.
- Clarifies the two revocation paths: supersession (inside `issue`) vs emergency withdrawal (this task, after which enforcers fail closed).

### Housekeeping
- Rebased onto current `main` (post #153–156). Rust + TS bindings regenerated on top; `trust-tasks-rs` and `@openvtc/trust-tasks` bumped 0.2.44 → **0.2.45** (lockstep), CHANGELOG entry, `Cargo.lock` refreshed.
- Version bumps / generated bindings may be rebased by the orchestrator as sibling consolidation PRs merge.

## Validation

- `npm run build` / `npm run validate` — **Validated 258 specs, indexed 46 shared schemas** ✅
- `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all` — 256 payload modules, diff committed ✅
- `npm run build-ts-bindings` — 304 TS modules ✅ (the TS generator emits request-payload interfaces only, so the `revoke` response change surfaces in Rust bindings only — consistent with existing generator behaviour)
- `cargo check -p trust-tasks-rs` — clean ✅

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Is a **claims profile** the right extension point on `vta/credentials/issue`, vs a new task family? (The design note argues the trust operation — step-up-gated, VTA-attributed issuance — is unchanged; only the claims shape is constrained.)
- [ ] Error-code casing: new code is `profileViolation` (camelCase per the pending #151/#152 convention) while this spec's existing codes are snake_case (`step_up_required`). Flagging the intra-file inconsistency for a call.
- [ ] Mandatory `credentialStatus` for the profile: comfortable making a published status list a conformance requirement for this credentialType while the base task stays consult-the-VTA?
- [ ] Distribution via `credential-exchange/query`/`present` with the VTA as holder of credentials it issued — acceptable holder semantics?

body:
Addresses https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/issues/852

Registry side of the confirm→task-consent consolidation (stream `s2-confirm-retire`). Implementation PR (VTI): **OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#858**.

## What changed

**1. New: `task-consent/granted/0.1`** — the notice VTI already ships but the registry never specced. Authored from the actual wire shape in `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/consent_request.rs::push_granted`:

```json
{ "status": "granted", "payloadDigest": "<salted wire digest>", "taskType": "<uri>" }
```

Executor → requester, fire-and-forget, no `#response` form (sync/event precedent). Proof **OPTIONAL** by design: the notice is non-load-bearing — the single-use grant lookup at re-submit is the real gate, so a lost notice costs one poll cycle and a spoofed one costs a refused re-submit. Only `granted` exists as a status: a denial is never announced, so this advisory channel can never be mistaken for the authoritative outcome.

**2. Additive: `task-consent/request/0.1` gains optional `note`** (in-place edit to the draft) — requester-authored display text, **explicitly untrusted**. The schema and prose require: attributed to `requester`, rendered visually distinct from `effects`, never treated as a statement of the task's effects, carried verbatim-or-not-at-all by the executor (whose signature attests provenance, never truth). This absorbs confirm's one legitimate use (a human-readable "why I'm asking").

**3. Retired: `confirm/request/0.1` → `supersededBy: task-consent/request`; `confirm/response/0.1` → `supersededBy: task-consent/decision`** (mechanism per `spec.meta.schema.json`: `status: retired` + `supersededBy`; the build enforces the pairing). Each Status section now carries the supersession rationale: a confirm is a task-consent with empty `effects` and `minApprovals: 1`, and confirm's requester-authored-`reason`-displayed-verbatim trust model is exactly the one task-consent exists to reject.

**Retired task URIs (for consumer sweeps, per the clean-cutover policy):**
- `https://trusttasks.org/spec/confirm/request/0.1`
- `https://trusttasks.org/spec/confirm/response/0.1`

**4. Housekeeping** — regenerated Rust + TS bindings; lockstep bump `trust-tasks-rs` and `@openvtc/trust-tasks` 0.2.43 → 0.2.44; CHANGELOG entry; refreshed `Cargo.lock`. Version bumps / generated bindings may be rebased by the orchestrator as sibling consolidation PRs merge.

## Validation

- `npm run build` — `Validated 258 specs, indexed 46 shared schemas.` ✔
- `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all` — 256 payload modules, no drift ✔
- `npm run build-ts-bindings` — 304 TS modules ✔
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs` — 294 + doc/integration suites, all passing ✔

## Coordination notes

- affinidi-webvh-service's dangling `confirm/request/0.1` reference is handled by the did-management stream (affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#143).
- OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin showed **no** trust-task URI references in source, but reviewers should confirm its approval UI doesn't render confirm prompts by other means.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] `note` quarantine language is strong enough — untrusted, attributed, never effects — and the carve-out in consumer rule 2 doesn't weaken the executor-authors-the-prose invariant.
- [ ] `supersededBy` targets (`task-consent/request`, `task-consent/decision`) are the intended slug-form (latest non-retired) references.
